title: Black Friday streaming deals 2026: The best deals live now and what to expect
summary: The best Black Friday streaming deals live include Paramount+, Apple TV, HBO Max, Peacock, and plenty of Prime Video add-ons.
content: The best Black Friday streaming deals: best streaming deal overall HBO Max Basic with ads $5.49/month for 12 months (save $5.50/month) Get Deal Best bundle deal Disney+ and Hulu Premium (no ads) $14.99/month for 1 year (save $7/month) Get Deal best ad-free deal Paramount+ Premium $2.99/month for 2 months (save $11/month) Get Deal best Prime Video add-on deal Apple TV (Prime Video add-on) $6.99/month for 6 months (save $8/month) Get Deal Best budget deal Peacock Select $29.99 for 1 year (save $60) Get Deal Best Roku add-on deal MGM+ (Roku subscription) $0.99/month for 2 months (save $7/month) Get Deal It's been yet another year of price hikes in the world of movie and TV streaming . Lots of our favorite streamers raised subscription costs in 2026, including Peacock, Apple TV , Disney+ , Hulu, Netflix , ESPN, and Paramount+ . Viewers everywhere are looking for the chance to save some money. Thankfully, a solution has arrived with this year's selection of Black Friday streaming deals. As Mashable's resident streaming expert, I've been tracking streaming prices for years now. There's absolutely no doubt that Black Friday is the best time of year to sign up and save on that wallet strain. I'm pumped that despite all of the price hikes in 2026, it's proving to be another banger year for streaming deals. I highly recommend taking advantage of these prices while they're available, particularly if you're looking to diversify your viewing and try out a new platform. The truth is that we're unlikely to see discounts this steep for a while. Most of the big streamers have dropped Black Friday offers, but we expect even more streaming deals to roll in during Cyber Week, which is the week after Black Friday. I'll be keeping a watchful eye out and will update this list as any other noteworthy streaming deals pop up. In the meantime, here are all the best Black Friday streaming deals live. Most of these deals expire on Nov. 30 (Cyber Monday), unless otherwise noted. Psst. Another thing to note is that most Black Friday streaming deals are limited to new and returning subscribers (meaning you haven't been a subscriber for at least a month). In most cases, you can't just cancel then re-subscribe at a lower rate, unfortunately. Black Friday 2026 live blog : Top deals, store hours, and real-time updates Best Black Friday streaming deal Opens in a new window Credit: HBO Max HBO Max Basic with ads $5.49/month for 12 months (save $66) Get Deal Opens in a new window Credit: HBO Max HBO Max Basic with ads (Prime Video add-on) $5.49/month for 12 months (save $66) Get Deal Why we like it The HBO Max Black Friday deal is top dog once again in the streaming world. This year, you can secure an entire year of streaming for half the usual cost. That drops it to just $5.49 per month, or $65.88 total for the year. Better yet, the offer is available as a standalone deal , a Prime Video add-on , or a Roku subscription . Yes, you'll have to watch with ads, but for the price, it's easy to look past that. With a Basic subscription, you also won't get access to live sports. Everything else is yours to enjoy — including recent box office gems like Backrooms , Wuthering Heights , and The Drama , as well as HBO Max's many excellent original series like The Pitt , The Comeback , A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms, and Industry. Best ad-free streaming deal Opens in a new window Credit: Paramount+ Paramount+ $2.99/month for two months (save $22) Get Deal Why we like it This year's Paramount Plus Black Friday deal is exactly the same as last year's. That's not necessarily a bad thing, though, as it's one of the only streamers to offer a deal on its ad-free tier. You can get two months of either Paramount+ Essential or Premium for just $2.99 per month (available as both a standalone deal and an add-on ). In other words, there's really no reason to not go with Paramount+ Premium. You save almost 80% compared to just 67% by going with Premium, and you get to enjoy your content ad-free. Not to mention, with a Premium subscription, you'll also unlock access to Showtime in its entirety, as well as your local CBS channel live. It's a no-brainer. Best Prime Video add-on streaming deal Opens in a new window Credit: Apple TV Apple TV (Prime Video add-on) $6.99/month for 6 months (save $8/month) Get Deal Why we like it Now that Apple TV costs a ridiculous $14.99 per month , it's harder to justify signing up for your own subscription. Thankfully, for Black Friday , the Apple TV Prime Video add-on and Roku subscription are both down to just $6.99 per month for six months. That's more than half off its usual cost, saving you a total of $48 over the promotional period. You'll have to either be a Prime member or a Roku subscriber to secure the discount. Apple TV's outstanding library is well worth the subscription, even if you cancel after the six-month promotional period. It's stacked with Emmy-winning TV series like Widow's Bay , Pluribus , and Severance , as well as Oscar-winning and nominated films, including Coda , F1: The Movie , and Killers of the Flower Moon. Best Black Friday bundle deal Opens in a new window Credit: Hulu / Disney+ Disney+ and Hulu Premium (ad-free) $14.99/month for 12 months (save $7/month) Get Deal Why we like it Disney has shockingly revived the exact same Black Friday bundle deals for Disney and Hulu from last year, despite raising prices across the board earlier this fall. If you're looking for the most bang for your buck and prefer to watch without ads, you can get an entire year of both Disney+ and Hulu Premium for only $14.99 per month. Considering an ad-free standalone Disney+ Premium plan typically costs $21.49 per month, the typical bundle price of $21.99 on a normal day is already an excellent deal. But this knocks an extra $7 off, getting you both streamers for less than the cost of one. You can also opt for the ad-supported plan and get both Disney+ and Hulu Basic for only $4.99 per month for a year, which is an even steeper discount. A Disney+ and Hulu bundle subscription is your ticket to the Super Bowl this season, as well as select live ESPN College Football games, the entire Skywalker Saga and most of the Marvel Cinematic Universe , new releases like Toy Story 5 , Hulu and Disney+ Originals, hit ABC TV shows, and so much more. Plus, you'll lock in a full year at a fixed cost, bypassing any potential increases once the upcoming merger goes live. Best budget deal Opens in a new window Credit: Peacock Peacock Select $29.99 for 1 year (save $60) Get Deal Why we like it Normally I wouldn't recommend Peacock's Select tier, as it's extremely limited in scope and not worth it for the usual cost. However, with this Peacock Black Friday deal, it's definitely worth a second look. At $29.99 for one year, which breaks down to about $2.50 per month, you'll get access to all of your TV favorites from NBC, Bravo, and more. It doesn't include Peacock Originals, hit movies, or live sports — in order to unlock access to those, you'll need at least the Premium tier. Fortunately, that tier is also included in the Peacock Black Friday offer. You can get Premium for $89.99 for one year, which saves you $40. $14.95/month (save $13.96/month) + get $20 Audible credit What deals to realistically expect from other streamers I'm going to be completely upfront about this: most streaming deals aren't going to change your finances in any significant way. The truth is that Black Friday streaming deals have gotten steadily less impressive over the past few years. It's also worth noting that most deals apply only to the ad-supported tiers (with a few exceptions). Still, any and every discount is welcome in a time when prices keep rising. Every cent counts, and it's easy to lose track of just how much you spend across various streaming services. Most streamers have announced their Black Friday deals at this point, but you may be wondering if there's more to come. Aside from some stragglers later this week, I would say the best streaming deals have already arrived. I'm shocked that Peacock's Black Friday deal is as good as it is for 2026. Last year, the streamer didn't offer a deal at all, so this is light-years better than I was expecting. If you've been holding off on subscribing, now is likely the only time you'll get a decent discount. The Paramount+, HBO Max, and Disney+/Hulu Black Friday offers are pretty much on par with their deals of years past. I would lock in HBO Max and the Disney+/Hulu bundle for a full year, as more price increases could pop up in 2027. Paramount+ tends to offer discounts throughout the year more than any other streamer, so if you miss out on this one, it's no biggie. It's not worth holding on for a Netflix Black Friday deal, unfortunately. Netflix has never offered a Black Friday discount, or any kind of discount for that matter. Netflix is the top name in streaming and obviously feels that it doesn't need to offer Black Friday deals. I don't expect this year to be any different, but I'm always willing to be proven wrong. It would be a nice and welcome surprise. We'll be updating this master list of the best Black Friday streaming deals throughout the week, so be sure to check back for updates.

title: Watch live sports for less with the Fox One 75% off Black Friday streaming deal
summary: Fox One's Black Friday deal is live. New and returning subscribers can save 75% on their first month of streaming.
content: SAVE $15 : Through Nov. 30, new and returning subscribers can score a month of Fox One for only $4.99. That's 75% off or $15 in savings compared to the usual cost of $19.99. The Black Friday streaming deal is available as a standalone subscription or Prime Video add-on . Opens in a new window Credit: Fox One Fox One (Prime Video add-on) $4.99 for your first month (save $15) Get Deal Opens in a new window Credit: Fox One Fox One $4.99 for your first month (save $15) Get Deal If you're a sports fan seeking a Black Friday streaming deal , Fox One is your best option this year. Through Nov. 30, you can get your first month of Fox One for only $4.99, which is a massive 75% ($15) savings compared to its usual $19.99 per month cost. While we wish the deal had been extended beyond one month, it's still a steep discount worth checking out. Make note that you must be a new or eligible returning subscriber to secure the deal. The Black Friday Fox One deal is available as a standalone offer, a Prime Video add-on , or a Roku subscription . All that means is if you subscribe through Prime Video or Roku, you'll be billed directly through those services instead of having a separate bill from Fox One. The Fox One library will live inside Prime Video if you choose to subscribe as an add-on service. What exactly does a Fox One subscription get you? A whole lot of sports, including live Sunday afternoon NFL games , Big Ten college football matchups , college basketball, MLB, NASCAR, and the list goes on. Sure, a month of streaming isn't that long, but you'll get access to a surprising number of games. This week alone would grant you access to the Eagles vs. Cowboys Thanksgiving Day game, West Virginia vs. Utah on Black Friday, in-market college football on Saturday, and in-market Sunday afternoon NFL games. When you're not watching live sports, Fox One also unlocks your local Fox station and Fox Entertainment on demand, including movies, TV shows (like MasterChef and The Simpsons ), and a bunch more. For $4.99, it's certainly worth a shot. Just remember to cancel before the month is up if you want to avoid the full charge.

title: Hurdle hints and answers for November 26, 2024
summary: Hints and answers to today's Hurdle all in one place.
content: If you like playing daily word games like Wordle , then Hurdle is a great game to add to your routine. There are five rounds to the game. The first round sees you trying to guess the word, with correct, misplaced, and incorrect letters shown in each guess. If you guess the correct answer, it'll take you to the next hurdle, providing the answer to the last hurdle as your first guess. This can give you several clues or none, depending on the words. For the final hurdle, every correct answer from previous hurdles is shown, with correct and misplaced letters clearly shown. An important note is that the number of times a letter is highlighted from previous guesses does necessarily indicate the number of times that letter appears in the final hurdle. title: The MGM+ Black Friday streaming deal knocks it down to just $31 for a whole year
summary: The MGM+ Black Friday streaming deal is impressive for 2026. New and returning subscribers get one year for $30.99 via Prime Video.
content: SAVE $31 : Through Nov. 30, new and returning subscribers can score an entire year of MGM+ for only $30.99 with Prime Video's Black Friday streaming add-on deal. That's 50% off the usual cost of an annual subscription. Opens in a new window Credit: MGM+ MGM+ (Prime Video add-on) $30.99 for one year (save $31) Get Deal The horror series From has made quite the splash over on Netflix recently. But viewers who want to keep the binge-watch rolling will need an MGM+ subscription in order to watch Season 4, which came out in spring 2026, as well as next year's fifth and final season. Luckily, thanks to Black Friday streaming deals , you can sign up for cheaper than ever. Through Nov. 30, new and returning subscribers can score an entire year of MGM+ for only $30.99 . That's 50% off the usual cost of an annual subscription and breaks down to only $2.59 per month. You can also choose a shorter subscription option and sign up for two months for just $1.99 per month (reg. $7.99 per month). Either way, you're getting a helluva deal. The catch is that you have to subscribe through Prime Video, which requires a Prime membership. The MGM+ streaming library will then live inside of your Prime Video app as a premium add-on channel and you'll be billed through Amazon directly. It's actually pretty convenient. As Amazon's niche service, MGM+ isn't exactly the most popular streamer around. But that doesn't mean it's not robust. Amazon MGM Studios films have recently started their streaming journey on MGM+ (rather than Prime Video), including Project Hail Mary , Is God Is , and Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother . It has plenty of other original series worth checking out beyond From as well, like The Institute , Secret Service , and Godfather of Harlem . MGM+ isn't the only streamer offering an excellent streaming discount this season. Be sure to check out our guide to all the best Black Friday streaming deals and follow along with all other Black Friday content in Mashable's hub .

title: Whats new to streaming this week? (Nov. 27, 2026)
summary: What’s new to streaming for the week of May 1, 2026, on Netflix, Prime Video, Hulu, and more? We've got you covered.
content: Looking for something great to watch at home? Streaming subscribers are spoiled for choice between Hulu , Netflix , HBO Max , Disney+ , Apple TV , Prime Video , Shudder , Paramount+ , Peacock , and more. And that's before you even look at the vast libraries of movies and television programs within each streamer! Don't be overwhelmed or waste an hour scrolling through your services to determine what to watch. We've got your back, whatever your mood. Mashable offers watch guides for all of the above, broken down by genre: comedy , thriller , horror , documentary , and animation , among others. But if you're seeking something brand new (or just new to streaming), we've got you covered there, too. 21. Way of the Warrior Kid Apple TV's Way of the Warrior Kid focuses on struggling middle schooler Marc (Jude Hill), whose classmates bully him relentlessly. When his Navy SEAL uncle Jake ( Chris Pratt ) comes to spend the summer with him and his mom Sarah ( Linda Cardellini ), Marc will get a chance to learn how to defend himself. SEE ALSO: Everything we know about Chris Pratt's 'Way of the Warrior Kid' To help his nephew, Jake puts together "Operation Warrior Kid." Based on Jake's own military training, his program is less about teaching Marc to fight, and more about teaching him to embrace true courage. Along the way, Jake will wrestle with demons of his own, as both he and Marc discover their own bravery. * — Belen Edwards, Entertainment Reporter Starring: Chris Pratt, Jude Hill, Linda Cardellini, Levi McConaughey, Ava Torres, Darien Sills-Evans, Carl McDowell, Parker Young How to watch: Way of the Warrior Kid is now streaming on Apple TV. 20. The Social Reckoning In 2010, Aaron Sorkin wrote The Social Network and David Fincher directed. For its sort-of sequel, The Social Reckoning , Sorkin writes and directs, while Jeremy Strong takes over the role of Facebook founder Mark Zuckerberg from Jesse Eisenberg. And all of this means a finger-wagging film that's more frustrating than revealing. Based on investigative reporter Jeff Horwitz's The Facebook Files , the film stars The Bear 's Jeremy Allen White and Anora's Oscar-winning Mikey Madison as Horwitz and whistleblower Frances Haugen, respectively. But the title is a bit of a misnomer, because what reckoning? SEE ALSO: What 'The Social Reckoning' misses about Meta Sorkin's political idealism is just one of his vexing indulgences, alongside his nostalgia for antiquated gender dynamics. In my review, I denounced The Social Reckoning as "misogynistic" and "unfunny," concluding, "Sorkin's dusty devices, problematic archetypes, and cringeworthy dialogue make the film feel instantly dated. Scroll on." — Kristy Puchko, Entertainment Editor Starring: Mikey Madison, Jeremy Allen White, Wunmi Mosaku, Betty Gilpin, Billy Magnussen, Bill Burr, and Jeremy Strong How to watch: The Social Reckoning is now available on digital. 19. Rob Lowe: The Outsider Having been a Hollywood star for decades, Rob Lowe's filmography meets people in different eras, whether you saw his 1980s Brat Pack breakout roles in The Outsiders and St. Elmo's Fire , revered his '90s smarminess in Wayne's World , or followed him down 2000s West Wing and 2010s Parks and Recreation hallways. Being an 18-year-old breakout star in '80s Tinseltown proved quite the start for Lowe, the focus of Netflix's new documentary directed by Chris Smith ( Tiger King , Sr. , Fyre ). Featuring interviews with Lowe as well as famous friends like Gwyneth Paltrow and Demi Moore, the film focuses on Lowe's chaotic life in Hollywood, through ups, downs, scandal, and stardom. — Shannon Connellan, Senior Editor How to watch: Rob Lowe: The Outsider is now streaming on Netflix. 18. On the Last Day of Christmas 'Twas the night before Christmas, when all through the house, demons invaded, so GTFO. That's essentially the set-up for On the Last day of Christmas , Paramount+'s festive horror film written and directed by Kevin Arbouet. Set in an apartment in Baton Rouge, Louisiana, the film sees Queen Sugar 's Tanyell Waivers as a mother whose yuletide celebrations with her teen son ( Way of the Warrior Kid 's Ellis Hobbs IV) are interrupted by sinister entities. — S.C. Starring: Tanyell Waivers, Ellis Hobbs IV, David Jensen, and Brandon Gilpin How to watch: On the Last Day of Christmas debuts on Paramount+ on Nov. 27. 17. The Trials of Karen Read The story of Karen Read began on Jan. 29, 2022, when her boyfriend John O'Keefe was found dead in the snow outside of the home of a friend. As a well-respected member of the Boston Police Department, O'Keefe was mourned by friends, family, and Boston as a whole. But when it came to how he died, two camps emerged. One — including the Boston PD — alleged he was killed in a hit and run, by his girlfriend Karen Read, and left to die in the snow. The other — spurred on by a podcaster known as Turtleboy — alleged that Read was being framed by O'Keefe's colleagues in an elaborate cover-up. This three-part Netflix documentary series from Danielle Johnson Cutts delves into both theories through interviews with O'Keefe's family, friends, and the most notorious investigator attached to the case. However, while Cutts includes plenty of archival interviews, she does not have new interviews with Read or Turtleboy, who both declined to participate in the doc. Cutts' investigation is thoughtful, thorough, and balanced. But don't expect big twists like Netflix's Unknown Number or outrageous interviews like The Crash . — K.P. How to watch: The Trials of Karen Read is now streaming on Netflix. 16. New Wave Here's a documentary you'll want to watch with the volume loud and proud. Directed by Douglas Tirola, New Wave is a four-part documentary series delving into the rise of the eponymous music genre from 1977 to 1987 and beyond. Its music was bouncy, bizarre, and massively influential. To explore New Wave's past, present, and future, Tirola brings together a jaw-dropping lineup of musicians for interview. Look at the featuring list below, for all the reason you need to tune in and bliss out. — K.P. Starring: Andy Bell (Erasure), Andy McCluskey (OMD), Annabella Lwin (Bow Wow Wow), Billy Idol, Bob Geldof (Boomtown Rats), Brian Ritchie (Violent Femmes), Brian Setzer (Stray Cats), Chris Frantz (Talking Heads, Tom Tom Club), Curt Smith (Tears for Fears), Danny Elfman (Oingo Boingo), Dave Wakeling (English Beat), Fred Schneider, Glenn Tilbrook (Squeeze), Jim Kerr (Simple Minds), John Taylor (Duran Duran), Johnny Marr (The Smiths), Kate Pierson (The B-52s), Kathy Valentine (The Go-Go's), Mark Goodman (MTV), Mark Mothersbaugh (Devo), Martha Davis (The Motels), Martha Quinn (MTV), Matt Pinfield (music journalist), Miles Copeland (IRS Records music executive), Richard Blade (DJ), Stewart Copeland (The Police), and Thomas Dolby How to watch: New Wave is now streaming on MGM+. 15. Andrew Tate: Toxic Empire With Andrew Tate and his brother Tristan currently in U.S. jail fighting extradition to the UK on charges of rape and sex trafficking, Andrew Tate: Toxic Empire delves into the backstory of the manosphere influencer. Cutting between archive footage of the Tate brothers and interviews with people in his circle and alleged victims, the four-part series from director/producer team Julian Hobbs and Elli Hakami explores how the Tates made their money — and the allegations they're currently facing. — Sam Haysom, Editor, General Assignments How to watch: Andrew Tate: Toxic Empire is streaming on HBO Max, with new episodes on Wednesdays. 14. Clashing Through the Snow Enemies-to-lovers Christmas rom-com with a job cuts edge, anyone? Michelle Randolph and Chris Briney lead Prime Video's Clashing Through the Snow as publishing editors Hannah and Ryan, who are fighting over one career-saving contract (nothing like redundancies in media to celebrate the holidays, right?) — and they've got to make it to New York in time. So, of course they'll be snowed under at the airport! Of course they'll have to share one rental car to meet deadline! Of course there'll be small towns en route to the big city to make them remember what Christmas is all about! Also, Paris Hilton and Julia Fox are in this, so there's something for everyone. — S.C. Starring: Christopher Briney, Michelle Randolph, Lukas Gage, Paris Hilton, Julia Fox, and PJ Byrne How to watch: Clashing Through the Snow is now on Prime Video. 13. The Slightest Touch Emma Fogarty and Colin Farrell's longtime friendship fuels Rachel Fleit's lauded documentary, The Slightest Touch , streaming on HBO Max this week. Living with Epidermolysis Bullosa (EB), Fogarty's condition means her skin is extremely fragile and can easily blister. However, she's determined to run the Dublin Marathon for her 40th birthday with her movie star friend, raising awareness for EB together. It's this important cause that sees Farrell inviting cameras into his personal life too, as Fleit explores this powerful, lasting friendship as parallel portraits. — S.C. Starring: Colin Farrell and Emma Fogarty How to watch: The Slightest Touch is now streaming on HBO Max. 12. Sesame Street, Season 57 Sesame Street is back with its 57th season! This timeless series is never to be taken for granted. Each episode brings family-friendly fun in the form of games, animation, original music, celebrity guests, and plenty of laughs with our favorite Sesame Street residents . This new volume (Volume 4 on Netflix) also promises more adventures with Elmo, Abby, and Tango. — K.P. Starring: Grover, Elmo, Cookie Monster , Bert and Ernie , How to watch: Sesame Street, Season 57 is now playing on Netflix. 11. The Holy Boy A creepy Italian village filled with smiling locals and an angel in human form are the ingredients making up The Holy Boy , Paolo Strippoli's horror about a teacher (Michele Riondino) who moves house only to stumble across a bizarre local tradition: In order to take their pain and sadness away, the locals all take turns hugging 15-year-old Matteo (Giulio Feltri). Fans of religious horror with a side order of telekinetic power may want to mark this one in their calendars. — S.H. Starring: Michele Riondino, Giulio Feltri, Paolo Pierobon, and Romana Maggiora Vergano How to watch: The Holy Boy debuts on Shudder on Nov. 27. 10. The Hunting Wives, Season 2 The Hunting Wives hooked Netflix subscribers everywhere with its deliciously trashy tale of rifles, wigs, and murder. Soon, it'll be time to head back to Maple Brook, Texas, where more ridiculousness (complimentary) awaits. Following the Season 1 finale, Sophie (Brittany Snow) and Margo (Malin Åkerman) have gone from lovers to estranged enemies. However, it's not long before their secrets and some new common enemies bring them back together. As The Hunting Wives continues to weave its web of seduction and gun-slinging, will these two hunters make it out alive? * — B.E. Starring: Brittany Snow, Malin Åkerman, Dermot Mulroney, Jaime Ray Newman, Evan Jonigkeit, George Ferrier, Karen Rodriguez, and Hunter Emery How to watch: The Hunting Wives Season 2 premieres Nov. 26 on Netflix. 9. The JLo Show This is probably the most bonkers title on our list this week, so all hail Jennifer Lopez, a consummate entertainer. A recording of her Las Vegas residency, The JLo Show features the American pop icon singing her hits, including "Jenny from the Block" and "I'm Real." But there's so much more. Surrounded by back-up dancers and snatched in the tightest, most glittery nude illusion bodysuits, Lopez also covers classics like "Let Me Entertain You" and recreates one of her big numbers from the bold musical bomb Kiss of the Spider-Woman . But that's still not all. Lopez also cracks jokes about her many marriages with an uncrackable face, and generally mythologizes herself through selected anecdotes. And that is still not all. SEE ALSO: Jennifer Lopez's 'This Is Me…Now' is A+ celebrity work Performing numbers reminiscent of West Side Story and Chicago, JLo also lets Broadway know what they're missing. Much like her wild autobiographical visual album This is Me...Now , The JLo Show offers Lopez doing too much, and being absolutely dazzling all the while. — K.P. How to watch: The JLo Show debuts on Paramount+ on Nov. 26. 8. The Tupac Tapes with Angie Martinez Remember how Curtis "50 Cent" Jackson produced a doc about Diddy that made the public reconsider the 1996 murder of Tupac Shakur (among other things)? Well, if you binge-watched Netflix's Sean Combs: The Reckoning, we wager you're already seated for The Tupac Tapes with Angie Martinez. This one focuses on Radio Hall of Famer and New York Times bestselling author Angie Martinez, as she looks back on her taped interview with Shakur, recorded in his Los Angeles home months before his death. In this four-part video podcast, Martinez plays portions of the tapes never heard before by the public. Plus, she discusses Shakur's life, legacy, and death with guests like Charlamagne Tha God, Joe Budden, Big Boy, Dream Hampton, RZA, and Wallo. — K.P. How to watch: The Tupac Tapes with Angie Martinez debuts on Netflix on Nov. 27. 7. Breeder It can be hard to get scientific research funded. And in writer-director Alex Goyette's horror Breeder , no one knows this better than MIT dropout Russell (Daniel Doheny). But it seems like his luck has changed when he finds an investor in Patti Kolb ( Glee 's Dot-Marie Jones), an affluent breeder of minature poodles. There's just one catch. She wants to meet him. In person. At her remote ranch. Where she's got a fleet of young women in residence. As you might guess from this setup (or the trailer above), Kolb isn't only interested in breeding dogs. And her methods for studs that don't meet her expectations are...harsh. It's little wonder that this mean indie has been gathering praise all summer long as it hit the film festival circus. Now you can see what horror lovers have been barking about. — K.P. Starring: Daniel Doheny, Dot-Marie Jones, Maddie Phillips, and Tanaya Beatty How to watch: Breeder is now available on digital. 6. Fjord Romanian filmmaker Cristian Mungiu was previously best known for his 2007 drama 4 Months, 3 Weeks and 2 Days . However, after winning the Palme d'Or at this year's Cannes Film Festival for Fjord, he's finding a new international audience, with a little help from the MCU 's Sebastian Stan. With a shaved head and bushy beard, Stan is unrecognizable from his role as the Winter Soldier. Opposite Norwegian film star Renate Reinsve ( The Worst Person in the World, Sentimental Value ), he plays a soft-spoken Romanian engineer, who's moved his wife and children to Norway to be closer to her family. But cultural differences hit hard, as the family's evangelical Christian devotion is seen as suffocating and even abusive by the children's teachers. When child protective services step in, Fjord becomes part family-drama, part crime-drama, inviting audiences to make their own decisions about right and wrong. — K.P. Starring: Sebastian Stan and Renate Reinsve How to watch: Fjord is now available on digital. 5. Tyson Fury Aside from holding titles from the World Boxing Council and the International Boxing Organization, British boxer Tyson Fury might be best known for his ferocity and endurance in the ring. However, his Netflix documentary, Tyson Fury , goes behind his tough exterior to reveal his tenderness. Interviews with his fighter father John Fury reveal a trying childhood, as well as the shocking revelation that challenged Tyson's idea of his dad. Director Lucy Wilcox also interviews his wife, Paris Fury, who gives insights into the boxer as a supportive partner and loving father. Wilcox's approach to Tyson is compassionate, giving him space to be vulnerable as he talks about his trauma, his self-esteem issues, and his struggles with suicidal ideation. And yet, she doesn't avoid touchy topics, like the public backlash over his comments about homosexuality and women. So, while this is an empathetic portrait of the fighter, it's also as hard-hitting as its subject. — K.P. Starring: Tyson Fury, Paris Fury, and John Fury How to watch: Tyson Fury debuts on Netflix on Nov. 27. 4. Wicker If you haven't had an entanglement with Wicker in regular unmoving cinemas or in rumbling 4DX , this is your chance to log it. Based on Ursula Wills-Jones' short story "The Wicker Husband," this raunchy, hilarious, heartwarming fairy tale sees a fisherwoman (Olivia Colman) requesting a basket weaver (Peter Dinklage) to literally make her a husband in order to spite the local townspeople (led by Elizabeth Debicki). And it works, with Alexander Skarsgård brought to life as a dashing wicker man. "It's a deeply silly, fairy tale concept," I wrote in my review. "But what directors Alex Huston Fischer and Eleanor Wilson have up their sleeve is a hilarious and heartfelt script, an incredibly talented cast, and magical production design...It's an artisanal Frankenstein tale, and one that will melt that brittle basket-woven heart of yours — or simply have you thinking about Taylor Swift's "Wood" differently." — S.C. Starring: Olivia Colman, Alexander Skarsgård, Peter Dinklage, and Elizabeth Debicki How to watch: Wicker is now available on digital. 3. Dig Amy Poehler reunites with Parks and Recreation co-creator Mike Schur for Dig , a charming sitcom based on Kate Myers's novel Excavations . Poehler plays Elise, lead archaeologist on a Grecian archaeological dig. When she makes the discovery of a lifetime, she'll team up with a crew of fellow passionate archaeologists to uncover it in secret, far from the prying eyes of egotistical dig head Neville (Hugh Laurie). While not always laugh-out-loud funny, Dig is a perfect warm and cozy watch, not to mention a wonderful character study of its wonderful core ensemble, made up of Poehler, Laurie, Geraldine Viswanathan, Antonia Thomas, and Fina Strazza. As I wrote in my review , "despite the flashy location and a new mystery twist, Dig retains the core formula that made Parks and Recreation so irresistible: investing deeply in a lovable new crew of unlikely friends." — B.E. Starring: Amy Poehler, Hugh Laurie, Geraldine Viswanathan, Antonia Thomas, and Fina Strazza How to watch: Dig premieres Nov. 23 on Peacoc k, with new episodes on Mondays. 2. Blade Runner 2099 You've never seen Blade Runner like you will in Blade Runner 2099 . The TV series upends the hierarchy of the prior Blade Runner films entirely. Following a brutal uprising, replicants are now in control of humanity. Now, replicant blade runners are in charge of hunting rogue humans — among these is Cora (Hunter Schafer). Tired of running, she undertakes a dangerous mission that forces her to pose as a blade runner. She'll soon cross paths with blade runner Olwen (Michelle Yeoh), a replicant with only days left to live. In those final days, she and Cora will search for a group of runaway replicants on the hunt for a secret that can change the world. Yeoh and Schafer are a match made in heaven, each handling Blade Runner 2099 's action with eternal cool. Their unofficial third co-star is the world around them, brought to brilliant life by the production team. Imposing pyramids and seedy shops shine under neon lighting and threatening dust clouds, while Vangelis-esque synths usher us into a sense of cyberpunk noir. It's a towering technical achievement fronted by two exceptional leads, and a worthy addition to the Blade Runner franchise. — B.E. Starring: Michelle Yeoh, Hunter Schafer, Dimitri Abold, Lewis Gribben, Katelyn Rose Downey, Daniel Rigby, Johnny Harris, Amy Lennox, Sheila Atim, Matthew Needham, Tom Burke, and Maurizio Lombardi How to watch: Blade Runner 2099 premieres Nov. 25 on Prime Video. Best of streaming this week: You Can See Everything Arguably the most talked-about movie of the year has landed on digital . And you better believe that's going to mean a fresh round of memes , spoofs , debates , and o bsession . When the teaser for You Can See Everything first hit, it seemed like a joke. Canadian comedian Nathan Fielder — of all people — interviewing notorious Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes in her home, ahead of her prison sentence? How could that be a real movie? The critics were raving ( me included ). But audiences did too, taking this A24 doc to record-breaking heights, and turning Holmes and her romantic partner Billy Evans i nto a national conversation. It's buzz has even reached space. SEE ALSO: Let's talk 'You Can See Everything' spoilers: An explainer for Nathan Fielder's Elizabeth Holmes documentary We're still saying the best way to see You Can See Everything is in theaters . But we're also giddy at the chance to be able to pause, rewind, and geek out with friends on a whole new level now that we have the remote. — K.P. Starring: Nathan Fielder, Elizabeth Holmes, and Billy Evans How to watch: You Can See Everything is available for purchase on Prime Video. (*) denotes a blurb came from a prior list.

title: Seth Meyers reacts to Fox News grappling with Trumps role in Huangs Nvidia return
summary: Seth Meyers examined Donald Trump's role in Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang getting his job back.
content: Donald Trump 's admitted role in getting Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang reinstated has Democrats and some Republicans in Congress promising to investigate . ICYMI Huang resigned after reports of multiple affairs , the CEO admitting one with an alleged Chinese spy . After Trump intervened with Nvidia's board, the CEO was reinstated , and Nvidia's stock (which the president owns ) then surged . Taking "A Closer Look" in his Late Night deep dive segment, Seth Meyers examined Trump's role in Huang getting his job back, notably in the same week he pardoned two turkeys ahead of Thanksgiving Day at the White House. "Trump got around to granting clemency to Freedom and Feathers, but it turns out those turkeys aren't the only ones he's thinking of pardoning," said Meyers. ( Trump told the New York Post that pardoning Huang for any potential crimes was "always an option," a day after telling CNBC the CEO "did nothing wrong.") SEE ALSO: Seth Meyers responds to Trump's AI meme of Jensen Huang But Meyers particularly responded to Fox News anchors struggling to defend Trump's intervention with Nvidia and Huang's subsequent rehiring, running through a series of clips in which hosts including Jesse Watters and Laura Ingraham, according to Meyers, "know how bad this looks." "Even the most hardcore Trump supporters can't defend the obvious corruption and self-dealing we can all see with our own eyes in the Nvidia scandal," said Meyers. "Trump won't help Americans impacted by high prices or tech outages or bomb-making chemicals in Iowa. But if you're Jensen Huang or Elon Musk, you get special treatment. The president will bend over backwards to help them out." Want more of the best of late night? Sign up for Mashable's Top Stories newsletter .

SEE ALSO: Mahjong, Sudoku, free crossword, and more: Play games on Mashable SEE ALSO: NYT Connections hints today: Clues, answers for November 26, 2026 Where did Wordle come from? Originally created by engineer Josh Wardle as a gift for his partner, Wordle rapidly spread to become an international phenomenon, with thousands of people around the globe playing every day. Alternate Wordle versions created by fans also sprang up, including battle royale Squabble , music identification game Heardle , and variations like Dordle and Quordle that make you guess multiple words at once . Wordle eventually became so popular that it was purchased by the New York Times , and TikTok creators even livestream themselves playing . Are you also playing NYT Connections? One tip is to select a word that includes at least two different vowels, plus some common consonants like S, T, R, or N. What happened to the Wordle archive? The entire archive of past Wordle puzzles was originally available for anyone to enjoy whenever they felt like it, but it was later taken down , with the website's creator stating it was done at the request of the New York Times . However, the New York Times then rolled out its own Wordle Archive , available only to NYT Games subscribers. Is Wordle getting harder? It might feel like Wordle is getting harder, but it actually isn't any more difficult than when it first began . You can turn on Wordle 's Hard Mode if you're after more of a challenge, though. Now AMC is putting its own spin on the movie recap. On Wednesday, Nov. 25, the theater chain announced AMC Stubs "That's A Wrap," a year-end look back at members' trips to the movies. This Tweet is currently unavailable. It might be loading or has been removed. How to get your AMC Stubs That's A Wrap In the comments on its announcement, AMC shared three steps: Open the AMC Theatres app and go to Account Settings . Tap Preferences . Check "Email me about promotions, offers, and more." AMC Stubs includes both the free Insider tier and the paid A-List subscription. When does AMC's recap come out, and what will it show? According to some Reddit threads, in 2024, some Stubs members reported getting a year-in-review email that counted their theater visits. Other members said they received a recap in December 2025. In the Instagram comments, one moviegoer was already bracing for a "time spent in a theater" stat. Another said they didn't need a wrap, they'd been keeping a spreadsheet all year. For now, anyone itching to see how many times they went back for the same movie can find their past tickets in their AMC Stubs account.

title: Best Buy is selling a $100 gift card for $60 on Black Friday — how to claim free credit
summary: On Black Friday, Nov. 27, My Best Buy members can buy a $100 Best Buy gift card for $60 in stores while supplies last (limit 1 per customer).
content: TL;DR: On Black Friday (Nov. 27), My Best Buy members — including free-tier members — can buy a $100 Best Buy gift card for $60 in stores while supplies last (limit one per customer). Opens in a new window Credit: Best Buy My Best Buy $100 gift card for $60 Get Deal at Best Buy If you are planning to brave the brick-and-mortar crowds for Black Friday, Best Buy has one of the easiest doorbusters to justify waking up early for. On Friday, Nov. 27, the retailer is selling a $100 Best Buy gift card for $60 — essentially handing out $40 in free spending money toward your next tech upgrade or holiday gift. That works out to a 40% discount on future Best Buy purchases, which can easily stack with existing Black Friday sale prices. Because quantities are limited and there are a few rules in place, here is everything you need to know before you head out on Friday morning. The $60 gift card deal is valid exclusively on Black Friday, Nov. 27, at standard Best Buy retail locations while supplies last. You cannot grab it online, in the Best Buy app, or at Best Buy Outlet and Pacific Sales stores. The offer is open to My Best Buy, My Best Buy Plus, and My Best Buy Total members. If you don't have an account yet, you can sign up for the free base My Best Buy tier online or in the app before heading to the register. Expect early lines, strict limits, and no rainchecks The promotion is strictly limited to one gift card per customer, and Best Buy is not offering rainchecks once a store's supply sells out. Best Buy stores are closed on Thanksgiving Day before reopening early on Friday morning (most locations open at 6 a.m. local time, though mall stores and local ordinances can vary), and individual stores may hand out tickets outside to manage lines for high-demand doorbusters. How to spend it (and what to know about holiday returns) You have to use the $100 gift card on a separate transaction, which just means buying the card first and immediately putting that $100 toward your next Black Friday pickup — like a new TV, laptop, or holiday gift. Purchases made from Oct. 30 through Dec. 31, 2026 are covered by Best Buy's Holiday Price Match Guarantee and are eligible for extended returns through Jan. 15, 2027 (excluding cell phones, AppleCare+ plans, and holiday decor). If you are mapping out a full-morning route, browse our rundown of Black Friday 2026 opening times before heading out (and confirm your local store's hours, just in case). You will also want to set up your free My Best Buy account ahead of time so checkout goes smoothly.

There are plenty of other bargains worth snapping up, as well, including price cuts on One Piece starter decks, KPop Demon Hunters cards, and Disney Lorcana sets. We've rounded up the best Black Friday trading card deals currently available across Amazon, covering everything from individual booster bundles to larger display boxes. Although, we'll also keep updating this guide as more offers go live throughout the whole BF weekend, so be sure to keep this guide bookmarked for the latest discounts. Best Pokémon TCG deal: 30th Celebration Tech Sticker Collection Opens in a new window Credit: The Pokémon Company Pokémon TCG: 30th Celebration Tech Sticker Collection $39.95 at Amazon $49.99 Save $10.04 Shop Now at Amazon With the popular 30th Celebration Booster Bundle now out of stock, the Tech Sticker Collection is the next best way to grab affordable packs from the Pokémon TCG's anniversary expansion on Black Friday — now as low as $39.95 at Amazon with a whole 20% off, or $10.04 off its current $49.99 list price. For that money, you’re getting three 30th Celebration booster packs, a foil promo card featuring either Lucario or Alolan Exeggutor, and a matching sticker sheet. You’re not only paying $13.32 per pack before counting the extra collectibles, you’re also only paying $6.24 above the Tech Sticker Collection’s $33.24 market price on TCGplayer . Best MTG deal: Marvel Super Heroes Play Booster Box Opens in a new window Credit: Magic: The Gathering Magic: The Gathering Marvel Super Heroes Play Booster Box $104.90 at Amazon $147.95 Save $43.05 Shop Now at Amazon Surprisingly coming in with a bigger price drop than ever for Black Friday’s trading card deals, the 30-pack box for Magic: The Gathering’s Marvel Super Heroes crossover expansion is now only $104.90 at Amazon . With that $43.05 price cut off the current typical price of $147.95, you’re only paying $3.50 per pack — and only $5.99 above TCGplayer’s estimated $98.91 market price . The lowest price Amazon has ever seen for this box (confirmed with Mashable’s price tracking methods), we don’t expect this deal to last very long in particular. Each booster contains 14 cards, including a traditional foil and one to four rare-or-higher cards, with the chance to pull special borderless variants featuring Marvel favourites like Iron Man, Hulk, and Doctor Doom. This box is even shipped and sold directly by Amazon rather than a third-party seller, although the listing is marked as a final sale. Best Yu-Gi-Oh! deal: Magnificent Monsters Box Set Opens in a new window Credit: Konami Yu-Gi-Oh! Magnificent Monsters Box Set $29.99 at Amazon $34.99 Save $5.00 Shop Now at Amazon Konami's Magnificent Monsters has hit a 90-day low on Amazon, now $29.99 instead of $34.99. That’s actually the lowest price this newly released box has ever been. If you’re a fan of the original anime series, this is a must-buy for grabbing revamped versions of classic cards, like Dark Magician and Elemental Hero Flamewingman. You get three five-card packs of Ultra Rares and three additional Secret Rares, each with a chance to upgrade to Starlight Rare. There are 18 reimagined anime cards to collect altogether. Best One Piece Card Game deal: Learn Together Deck Set Opens in a new window Credit: Bandai One Piece: Learn Together Deck Set (LT-01) $57.99 at Amazon $74.99 Save $17.00 Shop Now at Amazon If you've been curious about getting into the One Piece Card Game, this early Black Friday bargain is the best way to jump in, with Bandai's Learn Together Deck Set now down to just $57.99, down from $74.99 — a brilliant 23% discount. Built around Luffy, Zoro, and Nami, it includes three ready-to-play decks of 51 cards and 10 DON!! cards apiece. You'll also receive guides, storage cases, three five-card extra packs, and a two-player playsheet. Best KPop Demon Hunters Collectible Trading Cards deal: Energy Edition Opens in a new window Credit: Kayou KPop Demon Hunters card-Energy Edition-001-NA-Series 1-A $37.34 at Amazon $45.88 Save $8.54 Get Deal at Amazon It's an excellent time to get into the KPop Demon Hunters Collectible Trading Cards series, with Kayou's 12-pack Energy Edition reduced from $45.88 to $37.34 on Amazon in a limited-time 10% off deal. This works out to roughly $3.11 per pack, with eight cards in each. Unlike the Classic Edition, Energy Edition features 11 rarity levels, with 130 different card types to collect. These include the more sought-after SE cards, inspired by the song Golden , featuring laser-etched finishes and individual numbering from 1 to 366. There are also exclusive BP cards numbered up to 999, featuring HUNTR/X in their black stage outfits. Best Disney Lorcana TCG deal: Illumineer's Quest — The Great Hunny Rescue Opens in a new window Credit: Ravensburger Disney Lorcana TCG Illumineer's Quest — The Great Hunny Rescue $52.74 at Amazon $59.99 Save $7.25 Shop Now at Amazon For the early Black Friday season, Disney Lorcana's Illumineer's Quest: The Great Hunny Rescue has slipped to a mega-low price of $52.74 . Instead of opening packs, you'll be battling a self-playing Vine deck to rescue Piglet. The box has two prebuilt 60-card decks, a 50-card scenario deck, encounter cards, tokens, and a board. Play solo or with up to three friends, provided two bring their own decks. It's sold by Kings Games, shipped by Amazon, and marked as a final sale. title: Black Friday 2026 deals: Score free food from Burger King, Wendys, 7-Eleven, Krispy Kreme, and more
summary: The best Black Friday 2026 free food deals. Get free food from Krispy Kreme, Burger King, Wendy's, 7-Eleven, and more.
content: What do you think about when you consider Black Friday ? You probably go straight to deals on big-ticket tech items like TVs , power stations , and drones. And why wouldn't you? That's what Black Friday is all about. But there's something else about this massive shopping holiday that you should know about — it's also an incredible opportunity to pick up freebies. You can walk away with free gifts by shopping in-store , you can pick up free subscriptions , and you can even find free food deals for a limited time. That's right, popular restaurant chains are celebrating Black Friday by dropping BOGO offers, genuinely free giveaways, and limited-edition products. We've scanned the market to bring you a standout selection of our favorites: Black Friday 2026 food deals 7-Eleven On Black Friday, get a free large pizza when you place a 7NOW delivery order of $30 or more using promo code BLKFRI. Come back on Cyber Monday to save $25 off a delivery order of $50 or more with promo code LOADUP. Arby’s Loaded Rewards members can score any-size fries for $1 on Black Friday with a minimum purchase of $5. Baked by Melissa Save 25% on select 50- and 100-packs of bite-size cupcakes (excluding holiday items) when you enter promo code TREAT25 at online checkout. Baskin-Robbins Rewards members can take advantage of a BOGO offer throughout Black Friday weekend. Big Buns From Nov. 27 through Dec. 31, Big Buns is serving up its seasonal Santa's Slayin' Sweets menu, featuring $7.99 Grinch and Peppermint Shakes alongside a $3.49 Santa's Sundae. Biggby Coffee On Black Friday, grab a free 16-ounce hot or iced black coffee with any purchase of a Bragel or Maple Waffle Sandwich. Black Rock Coffee Bar Through Nov. 29, score free delivery on online or in-app orders totaling $12 or more. title: How Hinges deep-learning Most Compatible feature actually works, and how to train it
summary: It turns out you're probably using Hinge wrong — here's how to make it work in your favor.
content: Ever since its introduction in 2018, Hinge's "Most Compatible" feature has earned equal parts praise and scorn from online daters , who can't seem to decide if it's the best thing ever or a bad joke. Even today, eight years after it was first introduced, Most Compatible is a marvel of mathematical engineering, beginning with its foundation: the Gale-Shapley algorithm (also known as the propose-and-reject algorithm), developed all the way back in 1962 to solve a (hypothetical) mating problem. Hinge's variation of the algorithm works dynamically, constantly taking into account user preferences and choices to predict what kind of person you would most like to date. At the start of each new day, you will receive a Most Compatible profile suggestion that expires after 24 hours unless you interact with it. But there's a massive catch here that too many Hinge users are unaware of: your own actions and inactions are factored into the equation, so if you feed the algorithm bad data, it won't work in your favor, and you'll rarely see a compelling profile suggestion. We reached out to Hinge to gain a better understanding of their algorithm from the inside, and they described it as a "recommendation system" that combines multiple algorithms, "using your stated preferences and your activity on the app," to adjust and refine its suggestions. Here are three key tips from Hinge to help its recommendation algorithm work for you: Opens in a new window Credit: Hinge Hinge Learn More Be more picky Too many Hinge users (and men in particular!) cast a wide net, interacting with as many profiles as possible, sending out Likes all over the place. We get it: the more-is-more approach has its appeal, but it actually hurts the algorithm's effectiveness, since it becomes harder to narrow down your preferences when you're too indiscriminate about who you like or interact with. Or, as Hinge told us: "If you send too many likes, we can’t tell what you truly want. At the same time, if you rarely send likes, we don’t have enough information to learn from about who excites you. By engaging with others with curiosity and purpose, your recommendations meaningfully evolve alongside you." Instead of being overly enthusiastic in your search, be intentional : take your time to vet profiles and interact only with people you can genuinely see yourself dating. You may not even necessarily know what these profiles might have in common, but rest assured the algorithm will be at work in the background finding the common thread and refining its suggestions for you in the future. Refine your filters The default Hinge filters are very relaxed, but there's actually a Dealbreakers toggle hidden in the Dating Preferences section of your profile. The normal preferences (location and age range, for example) are taken into account but treated more like guidelines than hard limits. However, if you start enabling your Dealbreakers, Hinge will treat them as hard limits and never even show you profiles that don't match your preferences. As Hinge put it to us, "Hinge will only show you each other if you both meet the dealbreakers that either of you set, such as wanting kids. This helps you focus on people who feel like a real long-term match." The standard filters available to all Hinge users include age, gender, location, religion, ethnicity, and desired relationship type, but paying subscribers actually unlock even more potential Dealbreakers, including height, drug/alcohol use, political affiliation, and whether or not someone already has children, so premium Hinge users should definitely take advantage of these added filters to help the algorithm refine its suggestions. Fill out your entire profile Most dating app users, out of sheer eagerness to start browsing local singles, make a half-hearted attempt to fill out their profiles , usually doing the bare minimum to meet the app's requirements. But Hinge offers an extremely generous array of profile fields, and the more you fill out, the more data the algorithm can use to do its matchmaking work. And as Hinge pointed out to us, not answering a question is treated like a negative, actively shrinking your dating pool: "When you select 'prefer not to say,' it limits who can see you. From family plans and dating intentions to drinking habits, you're excluded from being shown to people who've set Dealbreakers around those compatibility factors." We recommend you put particular focus on filling out Hinge's prompts in a thoughtful way, taking particular care to choose ones that reflect directly on your personality or interests In Hinge's own profile guide , they offer important advice that is too often overlooked: ditch the clichés and one-word or low-effort responses, and take the time to give a personal answer to every question. And take the time to answer a voice prompt, as you'll be rewarded by the algorithm for doing so. Finally, there's good evidence that Hinge's algorithm rewards profiles with refreshed photos, so if you haven't updated your main photos in a minute, follow their photo refresh guide to optimize your new pics. If you follow the steps above, you should start to see the algorithm working more in your favor, and you'll look forward to each day's new Most Compatible suggestion.

Opens in a new window Credit: Lego Lego Up-Scaled Santa Minifigure $41.99 at Amazon $59.99 Save $18 Get Deal at Amazon It's the time of year when we'd usually celebrate Thanksgiving Day with the Macy's Parade. title: Target is giving away free gift cards worth up to $1,000 on Black Friday: How to claim
summary: On Black Friday, Nov. 27, the first 100 eligible guests in line at every Target store get a free Target gift card worth $25, $50, $100, or $1,000. Here is how it works.
content: TL;DR: On Black Friday (Nov. 27), the first 100 guests in line at every Target store get a free $25, $50, or $100 Target gift card — plus one $1,000 winner per store (no purchase necessary). Target is giving early birds a major incentive to set their alarms on Black Friday morning. On Friday, Nov. 27, the retailer is handing out free Target gift cards worth $25, $50, or $100 to the first 100 eligible guests in line at every store — plus one lucky shopper at each location will walk away with a $1,000 Target gift card. Unlike online doorbusters that disappear in seconds, this giveaway happens strictly in person and comes with a tight arrival and redemption window. SEE ALSO: Black Friday 2026 deals: The best store freebies from Kohl’s, Target, Lowe’s, and more Target stores reopen at 6 a.m. local time on Black Friday, Nov. 27. Showing up right at 6 a.m. will be too late if you want a free gift card. Target associates will start handing out prize redemption tickets to the first 100 eligible people in line roughly an hour before doors open (around 5 a.m. local time at most stores). Tickets are handed out on a first-come, first-served basis while supplies last, with a strict limit of one ticket per person. How to redeem your ticket Once doors open at 6 a.m. local time, you have to take your ticket to the Black Friday event cart inside that same Target store within one hour of store opening (by 7 a.m. local time at 6 a.m. locations). If you miss that one-hour redemption window, you forfeit your prize. Your card's exact dollar value is revealed when you redeem your ticket at the event cart. Out of the 100 winners at every store, 60 people get a $25 gift card, 30 get a $50 gift card, nine get a $100 gift card, and one person gets the $1,000 grand prize. Who qualifies and how you can spend it The giveaway is open to shoppers ages 13 and older (minors need a parent or legal guardian's permission to participate), and no purchase is necessary to get a ticket or claim a card. Once you claim your gift card, you can spend it right away on Target's Black Friday sale or save it for later in stores and online — just note that you cannot use it on prepaid or specialty gift cards. Anything you buy that's eligible also qualifies for Target's Holiday Price Match Guarantee through Dec. 24. Double-check your local Target's exact hours before heading out — and if you are mapping out a multi-store morning route, check out our guide to Black Friday 2026 store hours to see when other major retailers open their doors.

title: Moon phase today: What the Moon will look like on November 26, 2026
summary: See the Moon phase expected for November 26, 2026 as well as when the next Full Moon is expected.
content: The Moon is still looking almost full tonight, despite being a couple of days past the Full Moon. It's now in its Waning Gibbous phase, meaning the illuminated portion we can see is gradually getting smaller each night. What is today's Moon phase? As of Thursday, Nov. 26, the NASA's Daily Moon Guide tracker tells us the Moon is in the Waning Gibbous phase, with 96% of its surface visible. If you don't have any visual aids, you can still see the Mares Serenitatis, Kepler Crater, as well as the Tycho Crater. With binoculars, you'll also see the Gassendi Crater, the Endymion Crater, and the Posidonius Crater. And if you have a telescope, you'll get to see all this plus the Apollo 14 and 15 landing spots, plus the Descartes Highlands. When is the next Full Moon? In North America, the next Full Moon will take place on December 23. In other time zones it will fall on December 24. What are Moon phases? It takes around 29.5 days for the Moon to move through all its phases, according to NASA . Throughout this period, the Moon's position relative to Earth and the Sun determines how much of its illuminated surface we can see. Starting with a New Moon, the visible portion gradually increases until it reaches a Full Moon, before shrinking again as the cycle comes back around. The eight phases are: New Moon - The Moon is between Earth and the sun, so the side we see is dark (in other words, it's invisible to the eye). Waxing Crescent - A small sliver of light appears on the right side (Northern Hemisphere). First Quarter - Half of the Moon is lit on the right side. It looks like a half-Moon. Waxing Gibbous - More than half is lit up, but it's not quite full yet. Full Moon - The whole face of the Moon is illuminated and fully visible. Waning Gibbous - The Moon starts losing light on the right side. (Northern Hemisphere) Third Quarter (or Last Quarter) - Another half-Moon, but now the left side is lit. Waning Crescent - A thin sliver of light remains on the left side before going dark again.

title: Apple Watch Series 12 review: Same design, better health tracking, and more listening in
summary: The Apple Watch Series 12 delivers improved battery life (up to 51 hours), near-live heart rate tracking, and useful new features.
content: Looks are deceiving for the new Apple Watch Series 12 . On the outside, it appears to be the exact same smartwatch as last year (...and the year before that). But on the inside, it packs redesigned heart rate sensors and a faster S11 chip that enables intriguing new health-tracking features and AI tools, including the Siri AI beta. After wearing the Series 12 for the past three-ish weeks, I'm pleased to report that some of these invisible upgrades make a pretty meaningful difference — and that they don't chip away at the watch's battery life. My testing found that the Series 12 lasts slightly longer than the Series 11 from fall 2025. That said, I wouldn't miss half of the new AI-powered "Audio Intelligence" tools if Apple suddenly Thanos-snapped them out of existence. Always-on AI notetakers like Plaud, Pocket, and Bee are a growing trend in Silicon Valley, but they're not for me. Apple Watch Series 12 review: This looks familiar Here's the new light gold aluminum variant of the Series 12. Credit: Haley Henschel / Mashable The Series 12's external changes are primarily cosmetic. Apple added a ceramic case option to the mix again , giving buyers a new premium alternative to its aluminum and titanium variants (which now come in new shades like dark bronze and radiant gold). There are some fresh band styles and materials to chew over, too. For testing, Apple sent me a Series 12 with a light gold aluminum case and a sand Sport Band. I'm more of a silver girl myself, but it's very pretty. Each case type is available in 42mm or 46mm sizes, as usual. They're priced as follows: Aluminum case: Starting at $399 with optional cellular connectivity ($100 extra) Titanium case: Starting at $699 with cellular connectivity Ceramic case: Starting at $899 with cellular connectivity All of the Series 12's case options are still waterproof for up to 50 meters and carry an IP6X dust resistance rating, but Apple says the glass on the aluminum Series 12 is more durable than before. Otherwise, it's identical to the Series 11 (which was basically identical to the Series 10 ). Longtime Apple Watch users who are holding out for an exciting redesign might just stop reading here, understandably. If it's any consolation, we might get one next year . But as someone new to the wearable space, I will say this is a very attractive and comfortable watch. Familiarity breeds contempt, as St. Augustine or Taylor Swift or whomever once said. Apple Watch Series 12 review: Heart rate tracking got a huge upgrade The Series 12 can capture near-real-time heart rate readings thanks to its new Health Sensing System. Credit: Haley Henschel / Mashable Located on the underside of its base, the Series 12's new "Health Sensing System" is a cluster of advanced optical and electrical heart sensors. It has more electrodes that cover a larger surface area for better skin contact during ECG readings, rearranged photodiodes that are better at picking up light, and bigger, more efficient green LEDs that take readings way more frequently. While older Apple Watches only logged the user's heart rate continuously during workouts and every five minutes otherwise, the Series 12 now measures heart rate every five seconds throughout the day, no matter what you're doing. As proof, these near-real-time readings are available at a glance on a new heart rate watch face widget, or "complication." Credit: Haley Henschel / Mashable The Series 12's fancier sensors also up the frequency of its heart rate variability readings from every two hours to every five minutes. (HRV is a key stress indicator.) These changes make the Series 12's heart rate data much more precise and detailed than before, and more useful for non-athletes. In turn, other features that use this data should be more accurate, too — Vitals and the Exercise ring, to name a couple. I think this will be the Series 12's biggest selling point for most people. Finally, a Steps complication Apple reworked its pedometer model for the Series 12 to track steps more accurately when your arms are still. It also added a step count complication, aptly called "Steps." That one might not seem like a huge deal, but it actually resolves a common pain point with older Apple Watches: Users previously had to DIY a step-count complication by installing a separate pedometer app . It's great to see. Apple Watch Series 12 review: Readiness is dynamic My Readiness score started off at a 6 one day. Credit: Haley Henschel / Mashable It fell down to a 4 later that night after a very long walk. Credit: Haley Henschel / Mashable The Series 12 can now produce a "Readiness" score, a 0 to 10 rating of your capacity for physical activity based on your recent exercise, sleep habits, and Vitals. It needs a week of data before it starts working, FYI. I like that this score adjusts throughout the day — it's not a one-and-done daily reading. One of my mornings started at a 6 ("Ready") after a decent night's sleep. By the evening that same day, it had fallen to a 4 ("Pace Yourself") because I went on a long, brisk afternoon walk. That said, the feature mostly tells me what I could already figure out on my own. I don't necessarily need a score to know I'm less inclined to work out right after exercising. Athletes with more varied training regimens will probably get more value out of this feature than the average person. Apple Watch Series 12 review: I'm iffy on Audio Intelligence I got this Sound Recognition alert on the train. The Series 12 overheard the CTA's "doors closing" chime and confused it for an appliance's bell. Credit: Haley Henschel / Mashable The Series 12's four Audio Intelligence features use its built-in microphone to pick up on sounds and conversations. To address privacy concerns, Apple says it has ensured it doesn't create or store any recordings and that the raw audio is completely inaccessible before it's deleted. And if you're really weirded out by them, you can just opt out. Music Recognition with Shazam now works automatically. It usually takes only a couple of seconds to identify a song, depending on the amount of background noise, and it's always spot-on. Sound Recognition can alert you to sounds such as sirens, doorbells, smoke alarms, barking dogs, and car horns. It liked to confuse a train's "door closing" chime for an appliance bell, but was otherwise accurate in my testing. It's a useful addition for people who are deaf and hard of hearing. Here's a Live Rewind of a "conversation" I had with my dog, Pierogi. Credit: Haley Henschel / Mashable Live Rewind transcribes the tail end of a recent conversation when you double-press the Series 12's dial (aka "Digital Crown"). Apple says it can show the last 15 seconds of speech, but in practice it's closer to 10 seconds. Either way, it feels kind of pointless. It's such a short window of time that you might as well just ask the person you're chatting with to repeat themselves. It's also not correct 100 percent of the time. It once confused the phrase "pencil me in" for "Pennsylvania." Finally, there's Siri Recap , which is essentially a built-in AI notetaker. (It's meant for oral conversations, but it's also summarized TikToks I've watched and phone calls I've taken on speaker mode.) Its outlines are pretty macro and vary in their helpfulness depending on the conversation. I found it really good for recapping food orders and reviewing topics discussed in my Italian classes, but a little clunky when it comes to casual conversations. It doesn't distinguish between different speakers and sometimes mashes topics together. It's also not completely accurate — it said a friend named their baby "Popsicle" (no <3) — but it seems to be improving as I've continued to use it. This is a Siri Recap of a lesson from one of my recent Italian classes. It's accurate but pretty bare-bones — I took better notes myself. Credit: Haley Henschel / Mashable This Siri Recap covered a conversation my husband and I had with a friend over dinner. It lumped in our food order with a chat about his upcoming travel plans. Credit: Haley Henschel / Mashable I struggle with Siri Recap the most because it makes me feel like a creep. It doesn't alert you when it's listening in on a conversation, much less the person(s) you're speaking with, so it's on you to tell them that you're documenting your private discussions for later reference. (Awkward!) Keep in mind that such admissions will likely change the nature of your interactions: People edit themselves and put up their guards when they know they're being watched . Apple Watch Series 12 review: It's now a two-day smartwatch Apple rated the Series 12 for up to 24 hours of battery life, but in my testing, it's offered around 45 to 51 hours of normal use per charge. (Crucially, I haven't needed to activate Low Power Mode to hit those numbers.) This is a real testament to the S11 chip's power efficiency. It's also a nice bump from the Series 11, which Mashable's Stan Schroeder described as " a one-and-a-half-day smartwatch ." Apple says the Series 12 charges faster than its predecessor, too. I don't have a Series 11 handy to verify that, but I've been impressed with the Series 12's charging speed. Right before going to bed one night, I realized it didn't have enough charge for sleep tracking, which requires at least 30 percent battery. Luckily, just five minutes on an outlet bumped it from 23 to 39 percent battery. Apple Watch Series 12: The verdict Credit: Haley Henschel / Mashable With its latest mainstream smartwatch, Apple refines a familiar design with near-live heart rate tracking, noticeable battery-life gains, and a step-tracking widget — a small but welcome quality-of-life tweak. Audio Intelligence, meanwhile, takes a back seat to these more meaningful improvements. For most people, the Series 12 is the best Apple Watch to buy right now (unless, of course, you're willing to wait for next year's redesign). It's an easy recommendation over the more expensive Apple Watch Ultra 4 , which offers much of the same functionality but adds longer battery life and enhanced durability for outdoor and endurance activities. Compared to the budget-friendly Apple Watch SE 3, the Series 12 is also a more future-proof choice, with a considerably more comprehensive suite of health and fitness tracking features to boot. title: Black Friday Apple Watch deals are live, and theyre actually really good: Prices start at just $179
summary: Black Friday Apple Watch deals have landed, and they're surprisingly good this year. Get the Apple Watch SE 3 for just $179, or save $100 on the new Series 12.
content: The best Black Friday Apple Watch deals at a glance: Best Apple Watch deal overall Apple Watch Series 12 (GPS, 42mm) $299 (save $100 at Amazon) Get Deal Best budget Apple watch deal Apple Watch SE 3 (GPS, 40mm) $179 (save $70 at Amazon) Get Deal Best Apple Watch Ultra Deal Apple Watch Ultra 4 (49mm, GPS + Cellular) $649.99 (save $149.01 at Amazon) Get Deal Best Previous-Gen Deal Apple Watch Ultra 3 (49mm, GPS + Cellular) $549 (save $250 at Best Buy) Get Deal Black Friday sales are in full swing, and new deals are popping up every day. If you're in the market for a new Apple Watch, now's the time to get some serious shopping done: Every single Apple Watch model is now on sale for a record-low price . As of this writing, prices start at a mere $179 for the budget-friendly Apple Watch SE 3. Released in September 2025, the SE 3 added an always-on display while also maintaining its 18-hour battery life, meaning you don't have to make many compromises at all. And if you would like to upgrade to a wearable with more advanced health and fitness features, this fall's new Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 models are also heavily discounted. For Black Friday 2026 , our shopping reporters are closely monitoring prices at all the major retailers to make sure Mashable readers always know where to find the lowest-possible prices on Apple products, so keep checking back as we spot new Black Friday deals on Apple products . We'll get through this stressful holiday season together. Best Apple Watch deal overall Opens in a new window Credit: Apple Apple Watch Series 12 (GPS, 42mm) $299 at Amazon $399 Save $100 Get Deal at Amazon Why we like it Mashable recently named the Apple Watch Series 12 a Gift of the Year winner , and it's going to be at the top of many people's holiday wish lists. The Series 12 has all-new electrical and optical sensors that can take almost-live heart rate readings, giving you even more data for the revamped Vitals app. It also supports a new "Readiness" score that's useful for athletes with varied workout routines, according to our reviewer, and it charges faster than before. As of this writing, the Series 12 is down to a record-low price of $299 at Amazon and Walmart ( Target lists it at $299.99) — a 25% savings. We do not expect that price to get any lower. Read Mashable's full review of the Apple Watch Series 12. Best budget Apple Watch deal Opens in a new window Credit: Apple Apple Watch SE 3 (GPS, 40mm) $179 at Apple $249 Save $70 Get Deal at Apple Why we like it The Apple Watch SE 3 is the best model if you're not looking to spend big bucks on an Apple Watch. We were expecting this model to drop to $199 during Black Friday, but it actually dropped to only $179. In testing, Mashable reporters have found it excels at both sleep tracking and cataloging key health metrics, without feeling like overkill. Even though this smartwatch is under $200, it still has an always-on display and all-day battery life, too. As of this writing, Amazon and Walmart have the lowest price on the Apple Watch SE 3, so take your pick. Best Apple Watch Ultra deals Opens in a new window Credit: Apple Apple Watch Ultra 4 (49mm, GPS + Cellular) $649.99 at Amazon $799 Save $149.01 Get Deal at Amazon Opens in a new window Credit: Apple Apple Watch Ultra 3 (49mm, GPS + Cellular) $549 at Best Buy $799 Save $250 Get Deal at Best Buy Why we picked this In looking for the best Black Friday Apple Watch deals, we found great savings on both the Apple Watch Ultra 3 and Ultra 4. Apple's Ultra watches are designed for rugged outdoor use and performance athletes. They have astounding battery life, lasting up to three days in low-power mode. They also offer both GPS and cellular connectivity. The older Apple Watch Ultra 3 , usually $799, is now $250 off at Best Buy, and we've never seen this previous-gen smartwatch priced so low. Over at Amazon, the Apple Watch Ultra 4 is now on sale for $649.99, a $149.01 discount from the list price. The newest Apple Ultra Watch has even better battery life and more advanced health tracking; like the mainstream Series 12, it offers improved heart rate sensors and a Readiness score. To be honest, the Ultra 3 offers a lot of the same features thanks to the recent watchOS 27 update, but if you want the more future-proofed option, then opt for the latest and greatest version, i.e., the Ultra 4.
