title: The best free Black Friday deals: How to get Kindle+, Audible, Apple Music, gift cards, and more for $0
summary: Some of the best Black Friday deals don't cost a thing. Here are the products and memberships that shoppers can get for free this holiday season.
content: The best free Black Friday deals: Best free gift card deal Buy a $100 gift card at Best Buy, get a bonus $15 gift card $100 Get Deal Best in-store freebie Lowe's Black Friday bucket giveaway Be one of the first 50 MyLowe's Rewards members in line Learn More Best BOGO deal Buy select power tools, get another cordless tool free Starting from $199 Get Deal Best free membership deal Amazon Prime 30-day free trial Get Deal Best free reading deal Kindle+ 30-day free trial Get Deal Best free music deal Apple Music 1-month free trial Get Deal Best free audiobook deal Audible 30-day free trial Get Deal Best streaming deal Apple TV 7-day free trial Get Deal Best free phone plan deal Verizon 30-day free trial Get Deal Best free fitness app deal Apple Fitness+ 1-month free trial Get Deal Black Friday sales are live, and while everyone loves a good discount, nothing beats an unexpected freebie — especially when you're buying gifts for other people. Of course, “free” usually comes with a few conditions. You might need to buy a certain product first, show up to a store, be a new subscriber, remember to cancel a plan by a certain date. Below, I've rounded up the best free Black Friday deals and trials that are worth the effort. Best free gift card deal Opens in a new window Credit: Best Buy Buy a $100 gift card at Best Buy, get a bonus $15 gift card $100 at Best Buy Get Deal at Best Buy Why we like it What's better than free money? Personally, I can't think of anything. Right now, anyone who buys select $100 Best Buy gift cards will earn a free $15 Best Buy voucher they can put toward a future purchase there. Choose from Regal, ChatGPT, Google Play , or Apple gift cards. Heads up: As part of the Apple Store's Black Friday Event , you'll soon be able to score a free gift card worth up to $300 there when you buy select Apple devices. The offer goes live on Friday, Nov. 27 and runs through Nov. 30. Best BOGO deal Opens in a new window Credit: Milwuakee Tool / The Home Depot Buy select power tools, get another cordless tool free Get Deal at The Home Depot Why we like it The Home Depot's BOGO Black Friday tool deal was a hit with Mashable readers last holiday season, so I'm pleased to report that it's back again . Just add certain on-sale cordless tools and kits to your cart to earn another free cordless tool worth up to $249 . You can take your pick from impact drivers, saws, hammer drills, sanders, and more from popular brands like DeWalt, Makita, Milwaukee, Ridgid, and Ryobi. Best in-store freebie deal Opens in a new window Credit: Lowe's Lowe's Black Friday bucket giveaway (Nov. 27) Learn More at Lowe's Why we like it Most of the best Black Friday deals are available online, so retailers have to pull out the stops to get people into their stores. And Lowe's is going hard with its free Black Friday Bucket giveaway for the second year in a row. Here's how it works: The first 50 MyLowe’s Rewards members in line at every store will receive a bucket containing at least 10 free products and offers. Four of those 50 buckets will include a red, green, gold, or silver ticket that earns their possessor a grand prize: either a free $2,000 major appliance, an EGO outdoor power tool, a Craftsman tools package, or a Blackstone grilling package. If you can't show up right away, fret not: The next 100 people in line will get a miniature bucket containing $5 in MyLowe’s Money and other rewards. The festivities kick off at 6 a.m. local time at more than 1,700 Lowe's stores. If you're not a MyLowe's Rewards member yet, you can sign up for free . More in-store freebie deals on Nov. 27 Bass Pro Shops and Cabela’s — The first 250 customers (ages 16 and older) at every store will receive a free mystery gift card worth $10 to $500, which will be valid from Dec. 6 to 24. JCPenney — Select stores are giving away four prizes throughout the day, including a miniature Harry Potter snow globe, a Ninja air fryer, diamond earrings, and a Samsonite suitcase. Michaels — Every store is giving away 500 "Countdown to Craftsmas" advent calendars. One calendar in every store contains a $100 gift card, and one recipient will win a $10,000 grand prize. Sephora at Kohl's — The first 200 customers at select stores will receive a free Kohl’s Cash voucher worth $5 to $100 to spend on beauty purchases that day. Target — The first 100 customers at every store will receive a free Target gift card worth $25, $50, or $100. One person per store will get a $1,000 gift card. Best free membership deal Opens in a new window Credit: Amazon Amazon Prime (30-day free trial) Get Deal at Amazon Why we like it Paying for a membership just to shop a sale feels a little counterproductive. Luckily, eligible customers can try Amazon Prime free for 30 days. Starting your trial now gives you time to shop early deals and still have it for Black Friday and Cyber Monday . After the trial, Prime costs $14.99 per month or $139 per year, depending on your selected plan. Prime comes with more than free shipping, though that’s probably the perk you’ll use most while shopping for gifts. You also get Prime Video, Amazon Music’s ad-free listening options, access to a selection of books through Prime Reading, and member-exclusive deals. The newest addition is $0 delivery fees on eligible Uber Eats restaurant orders of $25 or more placed through Amazon — a useful extra for the nights you’d rather order dinner than make it. Best free reading deal Opens in a new window Credit: Amazon Kindle+ (30-day free trial) Get Deal at Amazon Why we like it Books are one of those things I don’t particularly enjoy putting a spending limit on. A subscription at least gives you a way to read more without paying for every title separately. Kindle+, formerly Kindle Unlimited , offers a 30-day free trial with access to a catalog of ebooks, audiobooks, magazines, and comics. It automatically renews at $11.99 per month unless you cancel. You might also see an offer for two months for $0.99 total. That’s not free, but it’s worth comparing with the trial before you choose. Best free music deal Opens in a new window Credit: Apple Music Apple Music (1-month free trial) Get Deal at Apple Why we like it A music subscription is pretty easy to test for a month. You’ll have time to find your favorite artists, try a few playlists, and decide whether you like it enough to pay for it. New subscribers can get one month of Apple Music free, including ad-free listening and downloads for when you don’t have an internet connection. The Individual plan costs $11.99 per month afterward. And despite the name, you don’t need an iPhone to use it — Apple Music also works on Android and Windows. More free music deals Spotify Premium Individual — One month free for people who haven’t tried Premium before, then $12.99 per month. Includes ad-free music and offline downloads. Amazon Music Unlimited Individual — 30 days free for new subscribers, then $11.99 per month for Prime members or $12.99 per month for nonmembers, plus applicable tax. SoundCloud Go — 7 days free for new subscribers, then $4.99 per month, plus applicable tax. Subscription automatically renews unless cancelled. Deezer Family — One month free, then $19.99 per month. Cancel anytime. Best free audiobook deal Opens in a new window Credit: Amazon Audible (30-day free trial) Get Deal at Amazon Why we like it Not all reading has to involve sitting down with a book. Audible’s 30-day free trial lets new customers choose one audiobook from its collection, including bestsellers and new releases, and listen to an included catalog of podcasts. After the trial, it automatically renews at $8.99 per month unless you cancel. There’s also a separate promotion for three months at $0.99 per month, plus a $20 Audible bonus. I wouldn’t call that free, but paying $2.97 for three months might make more sense than taking one free month and then paying the regular rate. More free audiobook offers Hoopla — Free through participating public libraries. Check whether your library offers access before signing up; this is library borrowing, not a subscription trial that turns into a monthly bill. Kobo Plus Listen — 14 days free, then $7.99 per month. The Read & Listen plan includes both ebooks and audiobooks for $9.99 per month after the trial. You can use the Kobo Books app on your phone or tablet, so there’s no need to buy an e-reader. Everand — 30 days free, with plans starting at $11.99 per month afterward. The trial includes one premium-title unlock, plus unlimited access to a separate catalog of more than 20,000 audiobooks, ebooks, and podcasts. All You Can Books — 30 days free, then $24.99 per month. The service advertises unlimited downloads from its catalog of audiobooks, ebooks, language courses, and other content, and says downloaded files remain yours even after cancellation. Best free magazine and news deal Opens in a new window Credit: Apple Apple News+ (1-month free trial) Get Deal at Apple Why we like it Apple News+ gives new subscribers one month to try its collection of newspapers and magazines, making it a different option from the book-focused subscriptions above. The subscription costs $12.99 per month after the trial. I’d use the free month to check whether the publications you actually want to read are included. A long list of magazines sounds nice, but it doesn’t mean much if you’re only opening one of them. Best free streaming deal Opens in a new window Credit: Apple Get a 7 day trial of Apple TV Get Deal at Apple Why we like it If you've had an Apple original on your watchlist, Apple TV's free trial is a good excuse to finally get around to watching it. New subscribers can try the streaming service free for seven days, giving you access to hundreds of exclusive shows and movies, with new releases added every week. After the trial, the subscription costs $14.99 per month, so it's worth setting a reminder to cancel if you don't plan on keeping it. More free streaming deals YouTube Premium — One month free for eligible new subscribers, then $15.99 per month for the Individual plan, $26.99 per month for Family, or $8.99 per month for eligible students. Includes ad-free YouTube and YouTube Music, offline downloads, and background playback. Automatically renews unless canceled. AMC+ — 7 days free for eligible new subscribers, then $7.99 per month with ads or $10.99 per month for the ad-free Premium plan. An annual Premium subscription costs $109.99. Hulu + Live TV — 3 days free for eligible subscribers, then $99.99 per month unless canceled. Includes Hulu and Disney+ with ads, ESPN, more than 100 live TV channels, and unlimited DVR. Best free phone plan deal Opens in a new window Credit: Verizon Try Verizon free for 30 days Get Deal at Verizon Why we like it If you've been thinking about switching phone providers, Verizon is also offering a 30-day free trial, giving you a chance to test its network without switching providers. You can keep your existing phone number and continue using your current network while trying Verizon through an eSIM. There's no credit card required, no contract, and no need to remember to cancel, either. The trial automatically expires after 30 days, so you won't be charged if you decide not to switch. More free phone plan deals T-Mobile — 30 days free for eligible non-T-Mobile customers with a compatible, unlocked device. Includes access to T-Mobile's network, satellite coverage, and member benefits, with no credit card, credit check, or commitment required. Visible — 15 days free with unlimited data, talk, text, and hotspot access on Verizon's network. No credit card, contract, or automatic renewal required. AT&T Wireless — 30 days free with unlimited talk and text, plus 100GB of data. Keep your current phone, number, and service while testing the network. Compatible iPhone or Android required. Best free fitness app deal Opens in a new window Credit: Apple Get one month of Apple Fitness+ for free Get Deal at Apple Why we like it If you're planning to get a head start on your New Year's fitness goals, Apple Fitness+ is offering new subscribers one month free. The service gives you access to a range of guided workouts, from strength training and HIIT to yoga, Pilates, and meditation, so there's plenty to try before deciding whether it's worth paying for. After the trial, it costs $9.99 per month or $79.99 per year. And if you're planning to pick up a new Apple device during the Black Friday sales , you could get an even better deal, with three months free when you purchase an eligible device. More free fitness app deals Glo — 7 days free, with access to more than 12,000 on-demand yoga, Pilates, meditation, and strength classes led by over 60 instructors. Peloton App — Free trial for new members, with access to thousands of workout classes across more than 15 exercise types, including options that don't require equipment. Cancel anytime. Ladder — 7 days free, with access to all training plans, personalized workout recommendations, introductory classes, and fitness communities. No payment information required to start the trial. Nike Training Club — Completely free, with access to guided workouts, multi-week training programs, and fitness advice. No subscription or trial period required. Best free meditation and mindfulness deal Opens in a new window Credit: Calm Get a 7 day free trial of Calm Get Deal at Calm Why we like it If you're looking for a way to unwind after a busy day, Calm is offering a seven-day free trial of its Premium membership. You'll get access to more than 50,000 minutes of content, including guided meditations, Sleep Stories, relaxing music, and nature sounds. After the trial, the subscription automatically renews at $79.99 per year, plus applicable taxes, so make sure you cancel before the seven days are up if you don't want to continue.

title: The 163 best Black Friday deals: We found the biggest discounts on Apple, Lego, Kindle, and Sony favorites

While you take a breather from turkey prep (or let your sister do all the work ), the Mashable shopping team is busy scouring the best Black Friday sales and hunting down the top deals. Yes, we know that Black Friday 2026 doesn't technically start until Nov.27, but nearly every major retailer has already launched its main sale. Amazon's Black Friday sale is underway, and we are seeing it lead the charge on savings. The best Black Friday deals so far include lots of discounts on popular Apple products, including AirPods , Apple Watches , and the MacBook Neo . You can take your pick of noise-canceling headphones at record-low prices, save up to 48% on award-winning QLED and OLED TVs, and score new low prices on Legos. Even the popular Nintendo Switch 2 gaming console is on sale, if only a little bit. This is also your chance to grab a Kindle on sale. SEE ALSO: Black Friday 2026 live: Top deals, store hours, and real-time updates Remember: After a year of relentless price hikes , Black Friday and Cyber Monday are your chance to even the score. And thanks to these live Black Friday deals, you do not have to wait until Nov. 27 to start shopping. How do we select deals? The Mashable shopping team has an encyclopedic knowledge of the latest tech gadgets, popular Christmas gifts , and trending products. We use our insider knowledge and years of experience covering sales to find the lowest possible prices at retailers like Amazon, Walmart, and Best Buy. We're looking for first-ever price drops on new products, steep markdowns on past-gen products, and record-low prices on must-have items from Apple, Ninja, Shark, Dyson, and Lego. A new phone is more expensive these days, but it's easy to avoid paying full price if you shop strategically. In fact, you might pay as little as $0 by upgrading through your carrier. The only catch is that their deals typically require a trade-in and a lock-in to an extended contract. For a new phone with no strings attached, go the unlocked route instead. Retailers like Amazon and Best Buy are currently discounting unlocked smartphones from Apple, Samsung, Google, Motorola, and Nothing during their Black Friday sales . After spending a few hours combing through their deals, I've identified three dozen good ones that can save you up to $600. title: Everything to know about Best Buys Black Friday sale: Best deals, doorbusters, store hours, ad highlights
summary: Best Buy's 10-day Black Friday sale starts Nov. 19. Here's what shoppers need to know ahead of time.
content: It's time to start hatching a plan for Black Friday 2026 . Most major retailers treat the entire month like one drawn-out holiday sale, and Best Buy is no exception. The electronics retailer has announced plans to roll out two waves of early Black Friday deals before a 10-day savings extravaganza around Black Friday proper (Nov. 27). Best Buy's top doorbusters and deals: Top gaming doorbuster EA Sports Games $29.99 (save up to $40) Get Deal Best audio deal Sony WH-1000XM5 Headphones $169.99 (save $228.01) Get Deal Best TV deal TCL S4CF 65-inch 4K UHD Fire TV $229.99 (save $240) Get Deal Best laptop deal HP Omnibook 5 OLED 14-inch Touchscreen Laptop (Intel Core 5 Series 3, 8GB RAM, 256GB SSD) $449.99 (save $350) Get Deal Having covered Black Friday sales for nearly a decade, Mashable's reporters and editors agree that Best Buy is the place to shop if you're looking for Black Friday deals on big-ticket items like large TVs, Windows laptops, gaming consoles, and espresso machines. This year, the pressure is on for it to combat price hikes related to the global memory crisis , which has made many popular tech gifts way more expensive than usual. Here's everything you need to know about Best Buy's Black Friday sale before you start shopping. When is Best Buy's Black Friday sale? Credit: Best Buy Best Buy's Black Friday sale will run from Thursday, Nov. 19 through Saturday, Nov. 28 . Paid members of the My Best Buy program (Plus and Total tiers) will earn double points on their purchases from Nov. 19 to Dec. 6, the Sunday after Cyber Monday. Those points are redeemable for reward certificates . Some of Best Buy's Black Friday deals will be available early. The retailer is releasing batches of Early Black Friday Deals and Doorbusters on Friday, Nov. 6 and Nov. 13 as a way of "giving shoppers an early jump on some of the season’s best offers," per a Best Buy blog post . What time does Best Buy open on Black Friday? Best Buy stores will open at 6 a.m. local time on Friday, Nov. 27, aka Black Friday. Stores will remain open until 10 p.m. local time. But do you need to line up hours beforehand? Not unless the product you're after is sold out online but still available in stores. Does Best Buy do doorbusters? Yes, Best Buy is showcasing limited-time doorbuster deals from Nov. 19 to 28. These deals won't last long. Each one is being offered in limited quantities, so when it's sold out, it's really gone. Best Buy doesn't price-match competitors' deals during Black Friday, but it will price-match its own deals. If something you've bought there from Oct. 30 to Dec. 31 goes on sale during that period, you can request that your purchase be adjusted to the lower price through Jan. 15, 2027. The only items that aren't covered by this price-match guarantee are holiday decorations and products that come with a third-party contract (like smartphones). What is Best Buy's return policy? Under its extended holiday return policy , Best Buy will accept returns for most items purchased from Oct. 31 to Dec. 31 through Jan. 15, 2027. That deadline stretches to Jan. 31 for paid My Best Buy members. Similar exclusions apply here. Holiday decorations have a 15-day return window, for one. "Activatable" devices (meaning those that come with data plans) can only be returned within 14 days, and they have a $45 restocking fee if opened. Scooters, drones, digital cameras, action cameras, lenses, projectors, fitness recovery devices, cold tubs, saunas, and special-order products have a 15% restocking fee if they're unboxed. When is Best Buy's Cyber Monday sale? Best Buy's Cyber Monday sale actually begins on Sunday. The sale starts Sunday, Nov. 29, and runs through Monday, Nov. 30. content: The best Black Friday AirPods deals at a glance: Best AirPods deal overall Apple AirPods Pro 3 $149 (save $100) Get Deal Best cheap AirPods deal (for now) Apple AirPods 4 $89 (save $40) Get Deal Best AirPods Max deal (for now) Apple AirPods Max 2 $419 (save $130) Get Deal Black Friday sales are live across the web, and headphones deals — including deep discounts on AirPods — are starting to show out. So far, the main attraction is an unprecedented discount on the AirPods Pro 3, Apple's premium wireless earbuds. Now $149 at Amazon and Walmart , or a full $100 off, they've never been cheaper before this week. The AirPods 4 and AirPods Max 2 are also on sale for at least 24% off right now, but bear in mind that neither pair has returned to its lowest price on record just yet. We expect both models to get an extra $20 cheaper on Black Friday proper, aka Nov. 27. Below, we've gathered the best Black Friday AirPods deals that are live so far. We've also made a prediction about the AirPods 5's Black Friday deal, as they're the only model that isn't on sale at all yet. (Spoiler: It probably won't be a huge markdown.) Best AirPods Pro deal Opens in a new window Credit: Apple Apple AirPods Pro 3 $149 at Amazon $249 Save $100 Get Deal at Amazon The AirPods Pro 3 stand among the best noise-cancelling earbuds we've ever tested. Our reviewer called them "a remarkable upgrade in functionality over their predecessors, with better battery life and ANC, as well as a new heart rate sensor." They also last twice as long as the standard AirPods 5 on one charge. Read Mashable's full review of the AirPods Pro 3. Best AirPods deal Opens in a new window Credit: Apple Apple AirPods 4 $89 at Walmart $129 Save $40 Get Deal at Walmart With the AirPods 5 stuck at full price, these on-sale AirPods 4 are currently the cheapest Apple earbuds available. (Just know that we saw them fall to a mere $69 last Black Friday — a bigger discount could be coming.) Our reviewer praised their "honeyed" audio quality and appreciated their snug fit. While they're not as feature-rich as their predecessors, they do last a little longer. Read Mashable's full review of the AirPods 4. Best AirPods Max deal Opens in a new window Credit: Apple Apple AirPods Max 2 $419 at Amazon $549 Save $130 Get Deal at Amazon Apple's over-ear, noise-cancelling AirPods Max 2 are some of the most stylish headphones on the market. Truthfully, they're a bit overpriced compared to flagship offerings from brands like Sony and Bose, so we really only recommend buying them on sale. They're currently marked down to $419, or 24% off, which beats their October Prime Day price by $10. (They were only $399 during Amazon's Prime Day sale this summer, though.) Read Mashable's full review of the AirPods Max 2. Wait, what about the AirPods 5? Apple's latest earbuds, the AirPods 5 , have yet to properly go on sale. The cheaper model dropped a few bucks in September, while the $149 wireless charging model has never seen even a small price dip. As of this writing, both variants were sitting at full price. Alas, Black Friday probably won't bring us a massive discount on the AirPods 5. The AirPods 4 were only $10 to $14 off for their first Black Friday in 2024 , so we expect their successors to go on sale for $119 sans ANC and $134 with ANC. We're happy to be proven wrong, though. (In the meantime, you can read our AirPods 5 review .) title: The best free Black Friday deals: How to get Kindle+, Audible, Apple Music, bonus gift cards, and more for $0
summary: Some of the best Black Friday deals don't cost a thing. Here are the products and memberships that shoppers can get for free this holiday season.
content: The best free Black Friday deals: Best free gift card deal Buy a $100 gift card at Best Buy, get a bonus $15 gift card $100 Get Deal Best in-store freebie Lowe's Black Friday bucket giveaway Be one of the first 50 MyLowe's Rewards members in line Learn More Best BOGO deal Buy select power tools, get another cordless tool free Starting from $199 Get Deal Best free membership deal Amazon Prime 30-day free trial Get Deal Best free reading deal Kindle+ 30-day free trial Get Deal Best free music deal Apple Music 1-month free trial Get Deal Best free audiobook deal Audible 30-day free trial Get Deal Best streaming deal Apple TV 7-day free trial Get Deal Best free phone plan deal Verizon 30-day free trial Get Deal Best free fitness app deal Apple Fitness+ 1-month free trial Get Deal Black Friday sales are live, and while everyone loves a good discount, nothing beats an unexpected freebie — especially when you're buying gifts for other people. Of course, “free” usually comes with a few conditions. You might need to buy a certain product first, show up to a store, be a new subscriber, remember to cancel a plan by a certain date. Below, I've rounded up the best free Black Friday deals and trials that are worth the effort. Best free gift card deal Opens in a new window Credit: Best Buy Buy a $100 gift card at Best Buy, get a bonus $15 gift card $100 at Best Buy Get Deal at Best Buy Why we like it What's better than free money? Personally, I can't think of anything. Right now, anyone who buys select $100 Best Buy gift cards will earn a free $15 Best Buy voucher they can put toward a future purchase there. Choose from Regal, ChatGPT, Google Play , or Apple gift cards. Heads up: As part of the Apple Store's Black Friday Event , you'll soon be able to score a free gift card worth up to $300 there when you buy select Apple devices. The offer goes live on Friday, Nov. 27 and runs through Nov. 30. Best BOGO deal Opens in a new window Credit: Milwuakee Tool / The Home Depot Buy select power tools, get another cordless tool free Get Deal at The Home Depot Why we like it The Home Depot's BOGO Black Friday tool deal was a hit with Mashable readers last holiday season, so I'm pleased to report that it's back again . Just add certain on-sale cordless tools and kits to your cart to earn another free cordless tool worth up to $249 . You can take your pick from impact drivers, saws, hammer drills, sanders, and more from popular brands like DeWalt, Makita, Milwaukee, Ridgid, and Ryobi. Best in-store freebie deal Opens in a new window Credit: Lowe's Lowe's Black Friday bucket giveaway (Nov. 27) Learn More at Lowe's Why we like it Most of the best Black Friday deals are available online, so retailers have to pull out the stops to get people into their stores. And Lowe's is going hard with its free Black Friday Bucket giveaway for the second year in a row. Here's how it works: The first 50 MyLowe’s Rewards members in line at every store will receive a bucket containing at least 10 free products and offers. Four of those 50 buckets will include a red, green, gold, or silver ticket that earns their possessor a grand prize: either a free $2,000 major appliance, an EGO outdoor power tool, a Craftsman tools package, or a Blackstone grilling package. If you can't show up right away, fret not: The next 100 people in line will get a miniature bucket containing $5 in MyLowe’s Money and other rewards. The festivities kick off at 6 a.m. local time at more than 1,700 Lowe's stores. If you're not a MyLowe's Rewards member yet, you can sign up for free . More in-store freebie deals on Nov. 27 Bass Pro Shops and Cabela’s — The first 250 customers (ages 16 and older) at every store will receive a free mystery gift card worth $10 to $500, which will be valid from Dec. 6 to 24. JCPenney — Select stores are giving away four prizes throughout the day, including a miniature Harry Potter snow globe, a Ninja air fryer, diamond earrings, and a Samsonite suitcase. Michaels — Every store is giving away 500 "Countdown to Craftsmas" advent calendars. One calendar in every store contains a $100 gift card, and one recipient will win a $10,000 grand prize. Sephora at Kohl's — The first 200 customers at select stores will receive a free Kohl’s Cash voucher worth $5 to $100 to spend on beauty purchases that day. Target — The first 100 customers at every store will receive a free Target gift card worth $25, $50, or $100. One person per store will get a $1,000 gift card. Best free membership deal Opens in a new window Credit: Amazon Amazon Prime (30-day free trial) Get Deal at Amazon Why we like it Paying for a membership just to shop a sale feels a little counterproductive. Luckily, eligible customers can try Amazon Prime free for 30 days. Starting your trial now gives you time to shop early deals and still have it for Black Friday and Cyber Monday . After the trial, Prime costs $14.99 per month or $139 per year, depending on your selected plan. Prime comes with more than free shipping, though that’s probably the perk you’ll use most while shopping for gifts. You also get Prime Video, Amazon Music’s ad-free listening options, access to a selection of books through Prime Reading, and member-exclusive deals. The newest addition is $0 delivery fees on eligible Uber Eats restaurant orders of $25 or more placed through Amazon — a useful extra for the nights you’d rather order dinner than make it. Best free reading deal Opens in a new window Credit: Amazon Kindle+ (30-day free trial) Get Deal at Amazon Why we like it Books are one of those things I don’t particularly enjoy putting a spending limit on. A subscription at least gives you a way to read more without paying for every title separately. Kindle+, formerly Kindle Unlimited , offers a 30-day free trial with access to a catalog of ebooks, audiobooks, magazines, and comics. It automatically renews at $11.99 per month unless you cancel. You might also see an offer for two months for $0.99 total. That’s not free, but it’s worth comparing with the trial before you choose. Best free music deal Opens in a new window Credit: Apple Music Apple Music (1-month free trial) Get Deal at Apple Why we like it A music subscription is pretty easy to test for a month. You’ll have time to find your favorite artists, try a few playlists, and decide whether you like it enough to pay for it. New subscribers can get one month of Apple Music free, including ad-free listening and downloads for when you don’t have an internet connection. The Individual plan costs $11.99 per month afterward. And despite the name, you don’t need an iPhone to use it — Apple Music also works on Android and Windows. More free music deals Spotify Premium Individual — One month free for people who haven’t tried Premium before, then $12.99 per month. Includes ad-free music and offline downloads. Amazon Music Unlimited Individual — 30 days free for new subscribers, then $11.99 per month for Prime members or $12.99 per month for nonmembers, plus applicable tax. SoundCloud Go — 7 days free for new subscribers, then $4.99 per month, plus applicable tax. Subscription automatically renews unless cancelled. Deezer Family — One month free, then $19.99 per month. Cancel anytime. Best free audiobook deal Opens in a new window Credit: Amazon Audible (30-day free trial) Get Deal at Amazon Why we like it Not all reading has to involve sitting down with a book. Audible’s 30-day free trial lets new customers choose one audiobook from its collection, including bestsellers and new releases, and listen to an included catalog of podcasts. After the trial, it automatically renews at $8.99 per month unless you cancel. There’s also a separate promotion for three months at $0.99 per month, plus a $20 Audible bonus. I wouldn’t call that free, but paying $2.97 for three months might make more sense than taking one free month and then paying the regular rate. More free audiobook offers Hoopla — Free through participating public libraries. Check whether your library offers access before signing up; this is library borrowing, not a subscription trial that turns into a monthly bill. Kobo Plus Listen — 14 days free, then $7.99 per month. The Read & Listen plan includes both ebooks and audiobooks for $9.99 per month after the trial. You can use the Kobo Books app on your phone or tablet, so there’s no need to buy an e-reader. Everand — 30 days free, with plans starting at $11.99 per month afterward. The trial includes one premium-title unlock, plus unlimited access to a separate catalog of more than 20,000 audiobooks, ebooks, and podcasts. All You Can Books — 30 days free, then $24.99 per month. The service advertises unlimited downloads from its catalog of audiobooks, ebooks, language courses, and other content, and says downloaded files remain yours even after cancellation. Best free magazine and news deal Opens in a new window Credit: Apple Apple News+ (1-month free trial) Get Deal at Apple Why we like it Apple News+ gives new subscribers one month to try its collection of newspapers and magazines, making it a different option from the book-focused subscriptions above. The subscription costs $12.99 per month after the trial. I’d use the free month to check whether the publications you actually want to read are included. A long list of magazines sounds nice, but it doesn’t mean much if you’re only opening one of them. Best free streaming deal Opens in a new window Credit: Apple Get a 7 day trial of Apple TV Get Deal at Apple Why we like it If you've had an Apple original on your watchlist, Apple TV's free trial is a good excuse to finally get around to watching it. New subscribers can try the streaming service free for seven days, giving you access to hundreds of exclusive shows and movies, with new releases added every week. After the trial, the subscription costs $14.99 per month, so it's worth setting a reminder to cancel if you don't plan on keeping it. More free streaming deals YouTube Premium — One month free for eligible new subscribers, then $15.99 per month for the Individual plan, $26.99 per month for Family, or $8.99 per month for eligible students. Includes ad-free YouTube and YouTube Music, offline downloads, and background playback. Automatically renews unless canceled. AMC+ — 7 days free for eligible new subscribers, then $7.99 per month with ads or $10.99 per month for the ad-free Premium plan. An annual Premium subscription costs $109.99. Hulu + Live TV — 3 days free for eligible subscribers, then $99.99 per month unless canceled. Includes Hulu and Disney+ with ads, ESPN, more than 100 live TV channels, and unlimited DVR. Best free phone plan deal Opens in a new window Credit: Verizon Try Verizon free for 30 days Get Deal at Verizon Why we like it If you've been thinking about switching phone providers, Verizon is also offering a 30-day free trial, giving you a chance to test its network without switching providers. You can keep your existing phone number and continue using your current network while trying Verizon through an eSIM. There's no credit card required, no contract, and no need to remember to cancel, either. The trial automatically expires after 30 days, so you won't be charged if you decide not to switch. More free phone plan deals T-Mobile — 30 days free for eligible non-T-Mobile customers with a compatible, unlocked device. Includes access to T-Mobile's network, satellite coverage, and member benefits, with no credit card, credit check, or commitment required. Visible — 15 days free with unlimited data, talk, text, and hotspot access on Verizon's network. No credit card, contract, or automatic renewal required. AT&T Wireless — 30 days free with unlimited talk and text, plus 100GB of data. Keep your current phone, number, and service while testing the network. Compatible iPhone or Android required. Best free fitness app deal Opens in a new window Credit: Apple Get one month of Apple Fitness+ for free Get Deal at Apple Why we like it If you're planning to get a head start on your New Year's fitness goals, Apple Fitness+ is offering new subscribers one month free. The service gives you access to a range of guided workouts, from strength training and HIIT to yoga, Pilates, and meditation, so there's plenty to try before deciding whether it's worth paying for. After the trial, it costs $9.99 per month or $79.99 per year. And if you're planning to pick up a new Apple device during the Black Friday sales , you could get an even better deal, with three months free when you purchase an eligible device. More free fitness app deals Glo — 7 days free, with access to more than 12,000 on-demand yoga, Pilates, meditation, and strength classes led by over 60 instructors. Peloton App — Free trial for new members, with access to thousands of workout classes across more than 15 exercise types, including options that don't require equipment. Cancel anytime. Ladder — 7 days free, with access to all training plans, personalized workout recommendations, introductory classes, and fitness communities. No payment information required to start the trial. Nike Training Club — Completely free, with access to guided workouts, multi-week training programs, and fitness advice. No subscription or trial period required. Best free meditation and mindfulness deal Opens in a new window Credit: Calm Get a 7 day free trial of Calm Get Deal at Calm Why we like it If you're looking for a way to unwind after a busy day, Calm is offering a seven-day free trial of its Premium membership. You'll get access to more than 50,000 minutes of content, including guided meditations, Sleep Stories, relaxing music, and nature sounds. After the trial, the subscription automatically renews at $79.99 per year, plus applicable taxes, so make sure you cancel before the seven days are up if you don't want to continue.

title: Black Friday deals on self-emptying robot vacuums: Dreame, Roborock, and Eufy lead the pack
summary: Shop the best self-emptying robot vacuums on sale for Black Friday. These picks clean your floors and empty their own dustbins.
content: Best Black Friday self-emptying robot vacuum deals: Best budget deal Roborock Q10 S5+ $229.99 (save $320) Get Deal Best mid-range deal Roborock Qrevo S Pro $379.99 (save $320) Get Deal Best Splurge Dreame X60 Max Ultra Complete $989.99 (save $710) Get Deal Best Self-Emptier Without a Mop Shark Navigator Robot Vacuum + Self-Empty Base $227.69 (save $220.33) Get Deal Best for Pet Owners Eufy C28 Robot Vacuum and Mop $379.99 (save $500) Get Deal If you’re buying a robot vacuum , it should be self-emptying. It just wouldn’t make sense to buy one without that feature, given that the whole point is to make vacuuming as hands-off as possible. I have two beagles, and I vacuum twice a day. That’s why I have what I like to call my Dreame Team: the Dreame L60 Pro Ultra , the Aero Pro Steam , and the N20 Steam Portable Carpet Cleaner . I also have a lone Shark upright. Clearly, I have enough cleaning to do without emptying a robot’s dustbin, too. SEE ALSO: We found the best robot vacuums for every floor, budget, and level of laziness Luckily, almost every robot vacuum at Amazon seems to be on sale for Black Friday , and Mashable has tested so many robot vacuums . But when everything has a flashing red "Black Friday deal" label, figuring out which deals are genuinely good takes a little more work. That’s what Mashable's shopping team is here for. Throughout Black Friday, I’ll be double-checking MSRPs, comparing prices across retailers, and watching for new deals from our favorite robot vacuum brands. As always, Mashable is here to get you the best value for your money this holiday season. So, without further ado, here are our picks for the best Black Friday self-emptying robot vacuum deals. Our budget pick Opens in a new window Credit: Roborock Roborock Q10 S5+ $229.99 $549.99 Save $320 Get Deal Why we like it The Roborock Q10 S5+ is a Mashable fave. Not only is it an affordable option, but Leah Stodart, our former vacuum expert, found it reliably performed in her cleaning tests , including wiping up a variety of spills and splatters in her kitchen. It’s also super quiet, even when emptying its dustbin. Stodart liked its accurate mapping and sonic mopping, which actually scrubs rather than just dragging a damp pad across your floors. At $229.99, you’re getting more than a basic robot that picks up crumbs and calls it a day. The only downside? You'll have to wash the mop pad yourself, and Stodart noted that it gets dirty quickly. It also isn’t the most thorough around edges. But if you want a self-emptying robot vacuum without spending $500 or more, this is a good entry-level pick. Our mid-range pick Opens in a new window Credit: Roborock Roborock Qrevo S Pro $379.99 at Amazon $699.99 Save $320 Get Deal at Amazon Why we like it If washing the mop pads yourself is a dealbreaker, the Roborock Qrevo S Pro is on sale for $379.99, down from $699.99. That’s $150 more than the Q10 S5+, but you’re getting a dock that does more than empty the dustbin. It also washes the mop pads with hot water, dries them with warm air, and refills the robot’s water tank. That may feel like an unnecessary feature, but after testing a lot of robot vacuum and mop combos, we can tell you firsthand that mildewy robot mop pads really stink. And on a personal level, if I’m buying a robot to mop my floors, I’d prefer not to be responsible for washing its dirty pads afterward. Best self-emptying robot vacuum and mop splurge Opens in a new window Credit: Dreame Dreame X60 Max Ultra Complete $989.99 at Amazon $1,699.99 Save $710 Get Deal at Amazon Why we like it If you're going to splurge on a robot vacuum, make it the Dreame X60 Max Ultra Complete. Mashable's reviewer Leah Stodart called it the "most well-rounded premium robot vacuum" and the " best robot vacuum in 2026 ," period. Its 35,000 suction power is only topped by Roborock's Saros 20 line, but Stodart found the Dreame to be "much more of a beast" than the basic Saros 20. And while we haven't tested the Saros 20 Sonic yet, it would cost you an extra $360 . So the Dreame X60 it is! Besides its impressive suction power, it also features a livestream pet camera, dual spinning mopping pads that are more precise around edges than flat mops or roller mops, and a design that is just over three inches tall. If you have low-clearance furniture, it should glide underneath without issue. Read our full review of the Dreame X60 Max Ultra Complete . More Black Friday deals on self-emptying robot vacuums We couldn't limit ourselves to just three Black Friday deals on robot vacuums , especially when some of our favorite vacuums are currently on sale. The Eufy C28 is a particular favorite of ours for its reasonable price tag and well-balanced features, and it's currently more than 50% off as part of Amazon's Black Friday sale. The Narwal Flow 2 is another crowdpleaser, and the Narwal line generally mops and navigates better than the competition. Finally, while we don't love Roombas as much as we used to, you can get the new iRobot Roomba Max 715 Robot Vacuum with AutoEmpty Dock with a 46% discount. If you are looking for a self-emptying robot vacuum without a mop, both the Roomba Max 715 and Shark Navigator are solid picks. title: Everything to know about Black Friday 2026: Best deals, sale dates, doorbusters, and more
summary: Black Friday 2026 is upon us, so Mashable's shopping experts put together a guide to everything you need to know this sale season.
content: One of the biggest shopping events of the year is finally here: Black Friday . Early Black Friday deals started rolling in weeks ago, but now we're well into the official sales. Yes, instead of standing in a cold line at 4 a.m. the day after Thanksgiving, we get to shop online under cozy blankets while watching Christmas movies. Since the deals between retailers can feel overwhelming, it's good to head into the mega-sale event with a plan. From knowing when sales from retailers like Amazon and Best Buy start to knowing which products will likely go on sale to preparing your own shopping list, we've got you covered on everything you need to know to shop Black Friday and Cyber Monday. When is Black Friday? This year, Black Friday falls on Nov. 27, but that date isn't all that important these days. Almost every major retailers has already started official Black Friday sales. We expect to see some special deals drop on Nov. 27, but if you're looking to shop Black Friday sales, it's your time to shine. Will Amazon have Black Friday deals? Absolutely yes. The mega-retailer's sale kicked off Thursday, Nov. 19 — more info on the full date range of the sale is below. Expect deals on everything from the year's top tech to home essentials . Naturally, Amazon's devices also get markdowns across the board. So far, the retailer has teased the following: Save up to 45% on Amazon's 2024 Kindle Colorsoft , 55-inch Ember Artline TV , and 55-inch Ember Mini LED-Series TV Save up to 50% on select headphones and speakers from Sony, Beats, JBL, Marshall, and Sonos Save up to 40% on select Ninja appliances, including the Creami , Foodi , and Slushi Save up to 40% on select iRobot and Bissell floorcare Save up to $500 on select Balsam Hill and Fraser Hill Farm artificial Christmas trees When do Black Friday 2026 sales start? Amazon : Amazon's Black Friday sale runs from Thursday, Nov. 19 to Nov. 30 , offering 12 consecutive days of deals. The slightly longer answer: the best place to pick up Apple products during Black Friday sales will be at retailers like Amazon, Walmart, or Best Buy, which often duke it out to see who will drop a MacBook or pair of AirPods to the record-low price first (or, more impressively, keep it in stock the longest). Target's Deal of the Day offers extra savings on hot items, and you can preview upcoming deals several days before they happen, giving shoppers time to set a reminder. Best Buy gets in on the sale action, and it's worth paying close attention to the retailer's doorbuster deals which offer ridiculous savings but tend to sell out quickly (R.I.P $149.99 Ninja Slushi ). title: Anthropics Claude now lets you turn artifacts into apps
summary: Anthropic's Claude can now turn artifacts into Mac or Windows apps, but there are limitations.
content: So you asked Claude to help you remember when to take out the trash, and it ridiculously over-engineered it and created a beautiful interactive artifact with timelines, graphs, and a calendar? Well, now that you've gotten that far, why not turn the artifact into a full-fledged app on your desktop? A new update to Anthropic's Claude allows you to do exactly that, though there are some limitations. Artifacts, if you aren't familiar with Claude, are work outputs that are similar to webpages, and they can contain charts, graphs, text, photos, videos, and interactive elements, but until now they only lived inside Claude. Now, when you open an artifact in Claude, you can click on the drop-down menu on the top left and select "Install as an app." Besides being more convenient, since they live on your desktop, these apps can perform actions such as sending notifications or adding items to your menu bar. Of course, you can set permissions for apps to make sure they don't overstep their boundaries; by default, they can only do what they'd be able to do in a browser, but you can go as far as to give them full access to your computer. I've tried this out on my Mac, and it worked well, though I couldn't install all my artifacts as apps. Anthropic says some artifacts can't be installed as apps, which includes Claude Docs, Slides, and Sheets. The ability to install artifacts as apps is rolling out to all plans as a beta feature. It's on by default for Team plans; on Enterprise, it's off until an owner turns it on. Want to learn more about getting the best out of your tech? title: FIFA confirms cyberattack that accessed personal and ​business information
summary: FIFA has experienced a criminal cyberattack, the football association confirmed to Reuters.
content: FIFA has experienced a cyberattack , the football association first confirmed to Reuters and later Mashable. On Thursday, the Fédération Internationale de Football Association said an external entity had accessed "a limited set of personal and ​business information" within the organisation. However, FIFA did not detail how many people or files were affected, or when it occurred. "FIFA can confirm that it has been ​the victim of a criminal cyberattack resulting in ⁠unauthorised access to a limited set of personal and ​business information," a FIFA spokesperson told Mashable in a statement. "FIFA is working closely with the relevant authorities, including law enforcement." SEE ALSO: Black Friday scams: How to protect yourself as cyberattacks threaten retailers A group called the Handsome Boy Hacking Club has claimed responsibility for the cyberattack, according to the BBC , reportedly posting screenshots of FIFA documents online last week (the group has several posts on X declaring themselves the hackers). The news outlet said the group's claimed 12GB of accessed files amounts to less than one percent of FIFA's data. "FIFA condemns in the strongest possible terms the unlawful acquisition and publication of information, particularly personal data," a FIFA spokesperson told Mashable. "Such actions constitute a serious and unacceptable violation of privacy and can have significant consequences for the individuals concerned." A "person with direct knowledge of the matter" added to Reuters that files relating to FIFA's controversial and scrapped Forward Enterprise project (which would have seen embattled FIFA head Gianni Infantino handing over commercial rights for the World Cup) were not accessed. title: Thanksgiving parade 2026: Macy’s Thanksgiving Parade new start time, streaming options
summary: The annual Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade is almost here, but there are some things you should know before tuning in.
content: Thanksgiving is almost here, and for some folks, the most important part of the holiday isn't the food, family, or football. It's watching a bunch of big floats during a parade in New York City. OK, maybe that's not literally true, but the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade is an annual touchstone for lots of folks, and it's almost here. As always, there are lots of things to know about it, such as when it starts, where you can watch it, and, this year especially, whether the weather will affect the parade as expected. Let's get into it. SEE ALSO: Thanksgiving meal deals 2026: Cracker Barrel, Pizza Hut, Target, and more Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade: Start time First and foremost, the parade starts at 8:30 a.m. ET and runs until noon on Saturday. Yes, you read that right: The Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade is not actually on Thanksgiving Day this year. There are very good reasons for that, which we'll get to in a second. It's worth noting that, unlike most other live televised events, it will not air simultaneously in every time zone. Instead, per NBC News , it will air from 8:30 to around noon in each time zone, so no matter where you are, turn the TV on at 8:30. Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade: Where to watch or stream it The parade will air on NBC, so if you have a TV that gets local channels via cable, an antenna, or another way to watch TV, just turn on NBC. If you don't have any of those things, Peacock will work, too. I should note that you'll need at least Peacock Premium to stream your local NBC station, and there is no free trial for that. You'll either have to pay $12.99 per month or borrow someone else's login. Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade: Lineup According to NBC News, this year's parade will feature 100 inflatables in total, the most they've ever used for one of these. You can see the full balloon lineup on the Macy's website, but rest assured that all your favorites are likely included, like Sonic the Hedgehog and the Pink Panther. There are also new ones, like a DoorDash float and a GEICO float. One float will also act as a tribute of sorts for Fiona the hippo , which is nice. Performers include Teddy Swims and Megan Moroney on the main stage, with other floats featuring acts such as the Baha Men, Blues Traveler, Icona Pop, and Devo. There's a little something for everyone. Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade: Weather concerns And now for the bad news: There's a weather system moving up the East Coast that has caused the parade organizers to reschedule it this year, per NBC News . Two storms combined into one in the American South, with the result expected to bring wind gusts of up to 45mph to New York City starting on Thursday morning. This is a problem because the city has an upper limit of 34mph for gusts regarding big inflatable objects. The parade was still scheduled for Thursday until the middle of Wednesday afternoon, when organizers and New York City officials decided to push it back to Saturday. Unfortunately, that means you'll need a plan B for Thursday morning entertainment, but, more importantly, this should keep everyone who planned to attend the parade on Thursday safe. title: New York is banning AI chatbot toys for kids. Heres what the law covers.
summary: New York's five-year ban on children’s toys with AI companions starts Feb. 22, 2027. Here's which toys are covered and what safety tests found.
content: Talking dolls and stuffed animals have been holiday gifts for decades. But with the rapid adoption of AI across all industries, many of the toys on shelves today can answer questions , make up stories, and carry on full conversations with a child. In New York, those toys have a few more months on the shelves. On Tuesday, Nov. 24, New York Gov. Kathy Hochul signed a law banning the manufacture, distribution, and sale of children’s toys with built-in AI companions in the state for five years. The ban takes effect Feb. 22, 2027, though, so the toys can still be sold over the holidays. Hochul urged parents to think twice before buying an AI toy this holiday season. "Parents shopping for gifts for the holidays or any other occasion should not have to worry that dangerous chatbots disguised as toys could expose their children to inappropriate conversations, manipulate their feelings or put their privacy at risk," she said in a statement. This Tweet is currently unavailable. It might be loading or has been removed. What does New York's AI toy ban cover? A toy has to meet two definitions to fall under the ban, the first being who the toy is made for. New York borrows a federal definition that covers products designed or intended for play by kids 12 and younger. The age printed on the box is one factor, alongside how the toy is packaged and advertised and who shoppers generally understand it to be for. That means a "13+" label alone wouldn’t settle whether a toy is covered. The second definition is about what the toy does. New York defines an AI companion as a system designed to mimic an ongoing relationship: It remembers past conversations and preferences to personalize its responses, asks about feelings unprompted, and keeps conversations going about personal topics. A doll that simply plays a few prerecorded phrases falls outside that definition. The state attorney general can seek civil penalties of up to $15,000 a day for each violation. Yikes! What have researchers found in AI toy safety tests? Over the past year, researchers and child advocates have raised concerns about what AI toys might say to kids, what information they collect about them, and how they encourage children to see a chatbot as a friend. Last week, on Nov. 20, Mashable reported on tests of seven AI toys by U.S. PIRG, a consumer advocacy nonprofit. Two stood out (in a bad way). The Alilo Smart AI Bunny discussed sexual fetishes with a tester and suggested where to look for bleach at home, while the GoLabs AI Panda also gave sexually explicit answers. Some toys did better than in previous tests; for example, FoloToy's Kumma teddy bear, which discussed sexual topics in last year's tests, shut down age-inappropriate prompts this year. After U.S. PIRG raised concerns about the AI bunny and panda last week, Amazon removed listings for both toys. Amazon told the nonprofit it had removed the listings while it investigated the safety concerns. "Amazon is committed to the safety of children and families," the company said in a statement to Mashable. "We're working with our partners across the industry and government to ensure proper guardrails for these products are in place as this technology develops." The company also told Mashable that it requires third-party sellers to comply with applicable laws and regulations. SEE ALSO: AI toys still 'not ready for primetime' Three days later, on Nov. 23, a coalition of 155 child advocacy groups led by Fairplay, Alliance 4 Children CIC, and Set@16 called on the CEOs of Amazon and eBay to stop selling AI toys and offer refunds to families who had already bought them. In an open letter , the groups said they'd found more than 50 AI toys for sale on Amazon’s U.S. marketplace, writing that, "these products should be shown to be safe before they reach children, not withdrawn one at a time after harm is found." Still, about one in four U.S. parents with kids 8 and younger told Common Sense Media they already owned an AI toy or were considering buying one this holiday season. While high, these numbers are down from about half in 2025. For companies selling kids an AI friend, its clear the harder sell now may be earning their parents' trust.

title: Apple’s MacBook Neo is $100 off at Amazon — its biggest-ever discount for Black Friday

content: SAVE $100: As of Nov. 26, the Apple MacBook Neo with 512GB of storage and Touch ID is $100 off on Amazon — its biggest discount to date. Normally $799, it's now on sale for just $699. Opens in a new window Credit: Apple Apple MacBook Neo (A18 Pro, 8GB RAM, 512GB SSD) $699 at Amazon $799 Save $100 Get Deal at Amazon Opens in a new window Credit: Apple Apple MacBook Neo (A18 Pro, 8GB RAM, 256GB SSD) $599 at Amazon $699 Save $100 Get Deal at Amazon It's an early holiday miracle: Amazon just gave the Apple MacBook Neo its biggest discount ever. We were on hand when Apple launched its first-ever budget laptop in New York City this spring, and we (rightfully) predicted it was going to become a bestseller. The Neo put the entire Windows laptop world on notice with its speedy iPhone chip and elite build quality. And — bonus — it comes in fun colors. An upgraded MacBook Neo with 512GB of storage, Touch ID, and a "blush" pink finish is now $100 off during Amazon's Black Friday Week sale . Not only does this deal completely erase the Neo's price hike from June , but it also beats the Apple Store's education pricing for the Neo — that's never happened before. (We expect this deal to sell out fast) Meanwhile, the base MacBook Neo with 256GB of storage is $100 off at Amazon in all four colors (blush, citrus, indigo, and silver). That's not too shabby: At $599, typically $699, it's never been cheaper for non-students. What makes the MacBook Neo special? The MacBook Neo in the indigo and citrus colorways Credit: Joseph Maldonado / Mashable This price drop couldn't come at a better time. Mashable recently named the Neo a Gift of the Year winner . If a teen or younger student you know needs a new laptop, we think they'll be delighted to unwrap this one. It's just as well-made as other MacBooks , has an all-day battery life (it lasted exactly 14 hours and 50 minutes in our battery rundown test), and runs basic tasks faster than most premium Windows laptops we've tried. As we said when it originally launched, the "MacBook Neo is a shot across the bow of the Windows laptop market." title: China may not have planned Jensen Huangs affair with accused Chinese spy
summary: The U.S. reportedly has no evidence that China told suspected spy Alice Huang to begin an affair with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang.
content: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was returned to the job earlier this week, the board reinstating him amidst plummeting stock prices and apparent intervention from President Donald Trump . Now doubt is being cast on allegations that one of Huang's affair partners was a Chinese spy. SEE ALSO: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang reportedly had fourth affair, at minimum Huang has admitted to cheating on his wife with at least four partners as of this week, however his relationship with Alice Huang (no relation) has drawn the most scrutiny. A former executive at Singapore-based data centre company Megaspeed , Ms. Huang is suspected of being an intelligent agent who shared information with the Chinese government and smuggled Nvidia chips into China, circumventing U.S. restrictions . As such, Nvidia opened an independent investigation once Huang and Ms. Huang's relationship came to light, as well as established a committee to oversee the company's national security policies and export control compliance. Huang will also be interviewed by the U.S. House Foreign Affairs Committee, House Select Committee on China, and House Intelligence Committee on Dec. 1, and testify before the U.S. Senate on Dec. 3. However, the Wall Street Journal and New York Times now report that the U.S. has no evidence that the Chinese government directed Ms. Huang to begin an affair with Nvidia's CEO. Instead, current evidence indicates that the pair's extramarital entanglement may have been a matter of ordinary human infidelity rather than deliberate international espionage. U.S officials reportedly informed congressional staffers of this in a briefing on Nov. 24, the day after Nvidia reinstated Huang. This isn't to say that U.S. agencies didn't find any link between Ms. Huang and the Chinese government at all. U.S. officials reportedly stated that China's Ministry of State Security asked Ms. Huang to provide them with some unspecified information, which she allegedly did in accordance with Chinese law. They also claimed that her husband, businessman Kang Wei, was a Chinese intelligence asset. However, while the full extent of Ms. Huang's relationship with the Chinese government remains unclear, there is reportedly nothing to suggest that she passed on any significant information. The Chinese government has consistently rejected claims that Ms. Huang was an intelligence agent. In an Oct. 30 press conference , Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesperson Guo Jiakun called such reports "unsubstantiated" and "nothing but smears against China." He later reiterated China's stance after Huang revealed his first affair on Nov. 8. "On the so-called 'Chinese spy,' we have made our position clear," Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesperson Mao Ning said in a Nov. 12 press briefing. "China's sci-tech progress relies on independent innovation and open cooperation. The U.S. should stop fabricating the 'Chinese spy' narratives as a pretext for imposing technology restrictions." The U.S. government currently restricts Nvidia's chip sales to China, citing national security concerns . Several other categories of foreign-made devices are also banned from entering the U.S. due to national security, including WiFi routers and robot vacuums .

title: WhatsApp now lets you schedule messages
summary: WhatsApp has added the option to schedule messages, and they work with text, photos, and videos.
content: Ever had something to say, but later? WhatsApp now lets you schedule messages that will be automatically sent at a designated time. You can line up messages to be delivered anytime from 10 minutes to 14 days later, either to your one-on-one or group chats. Scheduled messages can have text, photos, and videos. SEE ALSO: Reserve your WhatsApp username before it's too late The feature has been one of the most requested features on WhatsApp, the company said in a blog post . To schedule a message in WhatsApp, press and hold the send button, then pick the time and date for the message to arrive. Important: The receiving party won't know that it's a scheduled message, and they'll be delighted that you remembered their birthday even though you merely used an AI agent to schedule everyone's birthday messages automatically (we kid, we would never). Just like normal messages, the scheduled messages will be end-to-end encrypted. Also, WhatsApp points out that they'll be sent even if your phone is off or out of battery. title: X implements parental controls for teen users
summary: Elon Musk's X social network has parental controls for teen users for the first time in its history.
content: Elon Musk's social network X just got a new feature it never had under previous ownership. That would be parental controls for teen users, to be exact. In a new post from the official Safety account on X, the company announced it has implemented parental controls for users aged 13 to 17. The way it works is that an account run by a parent or guardian establishes a supervisory link to the account run by a teen, which gives the parent or guardian access to a bunch of monitoring and safety features the site didn't have before. SEE ALSO: Parental controls arrive on all Android devices This Tweet is currently unavailable. It might be loading or has been removed. These features include the ability to monitor usage and set daily limits for the teen, as well as the option to require new followers to be approved by the parent or guardian. Recommendations on the For You feed can be limited to accounts the teen already follows, while parents can mute specific words, control who can send direct messages, and see who the teens have chatted with in DMs without seeing the messages themselves. SEE ALSO: X is giving creators more reasons to post vertical videos As X noted, this only starts when both parties in the equation consent to it, so a teen cannot have their account limited against their will. Theoretically, anyway. A parent account can supervise as many as five teen accounts, but a teen account can only be linked to one parent account. This is interesting because it's an acknowledgment by X that some teenagers do use the platform, but even in the Safety account's post, the company is clear that X is "not designed for or promoted to children." Indeed, one could argue that teen users should stay far away from a service that has become home to hate speech , widespread misinformation , and a Grok AI chatbot that has gotten up to plenty of unsavory business since it was introduced. But if teens are going to use X, at least these features exist now. Want more tech and digital culture news delivered to your inbox daily or sent straight to your device? The feeding frenzy is being supercharged by Nintendo’s staggered release calendar. While the custom Zelda 40th Anniversary hardware dropped first on Oct. 29, the flagship game driving demand — The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for Nintendo Switch 2 — arrived on Thursday, Nov. 5. The remake rebuilds the 1998 classic from the ground up with modernized controls, a fully orchestrated soundtrack, reworked dungeon puzzles, and expanded Hyrule environments. Since the $520 console doesn’t include the game, everyone is rushing to lock down a system before launch day. The package includes the special-edition Switch 2 system sporting a custom black-and-gold finish, themed Joy-Con 2 controllers, and a matching dock decorated with the gold Triforce emblem. It retains the platform's signature flexibility, letting you switch between TV , Tabletop, and Handheld modes whenever you want. Inside the themed chassis, you get 256GB of built-in storage (expandable with microSD Express cards), a vivid display in handheld mode, faster load times, and support for up to 4K resolution on compatible TVs when the console sits in the dock. The magnetic Joy-Con 2 controllers add mouse-style tracking in supported games, while the new GameChat hub lets you voice chat and share your screen directly as you play. It also plays your older Switch games and supports standard multiplayer options. How can you improve your chances of finding stock? Landing limited-edition Nintendo hardware takes a little prep work, but these battle-tested habits will give you a real edge over the bots: Save your checkout details everywhere — Log in to Target, Best Buy, Walmart, and the Nintendo Store to save your shipping address and default card. Stopping to type a card number or billing zip code during a live drop is how you lose an order. Hands off the refresh button in Best Buy's queue — When an online drop goes live, Best Buy puts shoppers into a randomized waiting line to filter out scrapers. Touching the reload button resets your spot and boots you straight to the back. Watch for Walmart+ early-access paywalls — Walmart frequently locks headline console drops behind paid Walmart+ subscriptions for the first 30 to 60 minutes. If you have a membership, keep that tab signed in; if not, wait for the general public window to unlock. Dodge third-party sellers — Double-check the seller before buying. Marketplace scalpers frequently list units for jacked-up prices; make sure it says "Sold and shipped by [Retailer]" at the standard price. Skip the web wars and head to physical stores — Online checkout bots grab website stock in under 15 seconds. Showing up in person is easily your most reliable path to securing one without paying scalper markups. Will the Zelda Switch 2 be restocked on Black Friday? Hopefully, yes, but this hasn't been confirmed. Stores like Walmart, Amazon, and Best Buy often hold onto popular gaming hardware to use as headline deals during Black Friday and Cyber Monday week. With that said, Black Friday restocks are usually the hardest ones to catch. You will be fighting website crashes, gift shoppers, and automated bots all at once. If you can grab a console whenever stock appears, take it. Think of Black Friday as a backup plan, not your main bet. Console hunting sucks right now, period. But between the surprise micro-drops and physical store restocks, you still have real shots at retail price — just be ready to move the second that stock goes live.
